author: E.V. Odle
line: A body-implanted mechanism that lets its wearer control the flow of time.

name: Networked Telephone Answering Machine
author: H.G. Wells
line: Records spoken messages and lets the owner play them back by calling in from elsewhere.

name: Acoustic Apparatus (Osophone)
author: Hugo Gernsback
line: Delivers sound to the inner ear through vibrations in the skull.

name: Wireless Access Point
author: H.G. Wells
line: Infrastructure that beams both electricity and data through the air to nearby devices.

name: Parallel Universe
author: H.G. Wells
line: A separate reality existing alongside ours that one might visit.

name: Blaster
author: Nictzin Dyalhis
line: A weapon firing an energy beam that wrecks anything it hits.

name: Quadraturin
author: Sigizmund Krzhizhanowsky
line: A coating that enlarges a room's interior without changing its outside.

name: Atomic Energy Motor
author: G. Peyton Wertenbaker
line: A motor that draws its power from nuclear reactions.

name: Artificial Brain
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A synthetic thinking machine whose architecture copies the human brain.

name: Bolognium
work: Transactions of Amer Soc for Steel Treating
author: Edgar Bain
line: A made-up chemical element coined humorously by metallurgists, with no defined uses.

name: Robot Wheel
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A gigantic self-driving machine shaped like a single rolling wheel.

name: Artificial Life
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: Builds living organisms out of non-living chemical ingredients.

name: Atomic Machine
author: G. Peyton Wertenbaker
line: A wearable device that makes its user grow or shrink in size.

name: Flexible Metal Arms (Tentacles)
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: Bendable mechanical limbs that curl and grip like an octopus's arms.

name: Starship
author: Raymond Quiex
line: A craft that carries people or cargo through space.

name: Transparent Dome Helmet
author: G. Peyton Wertenbaker
line: A clear bubble helmet that seals a space suit while letting the wearer look around.

name: Tentacle Machines
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: Huge self-directed machines with cylinder bodies and snaking arms.

name: Blue Ray of Death
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A beam that instantly burns a living creature to ash.

name: Gyro-Hat
author: Ellis Parker Butler
line: A spinning gyroscope hidden in a hat that keeps its wearer from swaying or falling.

name: Vacuum Suit
author: G. Peyton Wertenbaker
line: A sealed garment that keeps a person alive in airless space.

name: Computer Vision (Artificial Eye)
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: Gives a computer the ability to see and interpret images through a camera.

name: Paralyzing Cone
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A weapon that locks up a target's muscles so they cannot move.

name: Cold Ray
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A beam that drains heat from whatever it is pointed at.

name: Repulsor Ray
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: Pushes a craft forward by expelling a stream of charged particles.

name: Harvest Power From Stray Energy
author: Harl Vincent
line: Gathers ambient electrical energy from the surroundings to run a small device.

name: Death-Beam
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: Bright energy beams fired between ships in space combat.

name: Steering a Star
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: Pushes a whole star off its natural course and moves it somewhere else.

name: Repellor Anti-Gravity Rays
author: Philip Frances Nowlan
line: A beam that counteracts gravity to hold aircraft aloft over a planet.

name: Anti-Gravity Belt
author: Philip Frances Nowlan
line: A worn belt that lessens the pull of gravity on its wearer.

name: Meteorometer
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: Warns a spacecraft of incoming meteors in its path.

name: Floater
author: Philip Frances Nowlan
line: Lets a person hover in mid-air with no visible support.

name: Auto-Car
author: David H. Keller
line: A small personal vehicle a person can drive both inside buildings and on streets.

name: Hall of the Council
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A vast assembly chamber built to seat representatives from across a galaxy.

name: Atoplane
author: Earl L. Bell
line: A nuclear-powered aeroplane that flies very fast over huge ranges.

name: Airlock
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: A sealed chamber between a spacecraft's interior and outer space for safe passage.

name: Ultraphone Ear-Disc
author: Philip Frances Nowlan
line: Wireless earpieces that sit on the ears and cut out background noise.

name: Needle Pipe
author: Ray Cummings
line: A weapon that fires metal splinters at nearly the speed of light.

name: Mother World
author: Earl L. Bell
line: A term for the planet where a species or person originated.

name: Ultrophone
author: Philip Frances Nowlan
line: A radio link letting both sides talk and listen at the same moment.

name: Videophone
author: Harl Vincent
line: A personal link that sends pictures along with voices between two people.

name: Telestereo
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A round screen showing a live image of someone calling from far away.

name: Psycho-Phone
author: David H. Keller
line: Captures a person's thoughts and replays them later.

name: Space-Lanes
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: Established routes that spacecraft routinely follow.

name: Psychophonic Nurse
author: David H. Keller
line: A robot that looks after infants and young children.

name: Atomic Percolator
author: Harl Vincent
line: Brews coffee using heat from radioactive material.

name: Space Buoy
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A beacon placed in space to mark a location for navigators.

name: Hyper-space
author: Kirk Meadowcroft
line: An alternative realm where ships can journey faster than light.

name: Pressure-Suit
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: A sealed, pressurised outfit that protects a person in vacuum.

name: Flying Harness
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: A strap-on rig that lets its wearer fly around freely.

name: Attractive Ray
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A beam that draws objects toward its source.

name: Inertron
author: Philip Frances Nowlan
line: A metal that behaves like dense heavy metals yet weighs far less.

name: Vibration-Propelled Cruiser
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A spaceship propelled by making ripples in the fabric of spacetime.

name: Neutralizing Wall
author: Harl Vincent
line: A barrier that blocks electrical and mechanical disturbances so whatever lies behind it cannot be detected.

name: Heat Transmitter
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: Collects sunlight near the sun and sends it as focused energy to distant, colder planets.

name: Universal Sterilization Law
author: David H. Keller
line: A policy that makes every young person infertile and replaces births with laboratory-made people.

name: Telechart
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A touch-sensitive panel that displays star positions for plotting courses between stars.

name: Concentro
author: Philip Frances Nowlan
line: Compact manufactured food packs for soldiers and travellers.

name: Pain Ray
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A weapon that causes intense pain by stimulating nerves from a distance.

name: Private Space Cruiser
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A spacecraft owned and flown by a private party rather than a government.

name: Grantline Comptometer
author: Ray Cummings
line: A keyboard calculating machine that solves advanced maths like calculus with ease.

name: Jumper
author: Philip Frances Nowlan
line: A belt that cancels its wearer's weight so they can leap huge distances.

name: Negative Acceleration
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: Flipping a rocket around and firing its engine forward to slow down.

name: Meteor-Sweeps
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: Operations that hunt down and blast apart dangerous meteor swarms to keep space routes safe.

name: Gravity-Screen
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A shield that blocks gravity's pull on whatever sits behind it.

name: Ultron Wire
author: Philip Frances Nowlan
line: An extremely thin, very strong wire so fine it cannot be seen.

name: Chest Disc
author: Philip Frances Nowlan
line: A chest-worn radio that transmits whenever the wearer speaks.

name: Electric Diaper
author: David H. Keller
line: A nappy that signals when it needs changing.

name: Ultron
author: Philip Frances Nowlan
line: A substance that neither reflects light nor can be seen at all.

name: Rocket Gun
author: Philip Frances Nowlan
line: A shoulder-fired launcher that shoots small rockets.

name: Disintegrator Ray (Dis Ray)
author: Philip Frances Nowlan
line: A beam that makes matter vanish entirely.

name: Raytron Apparatus
author: Ray Cummings
line: An airborne camera that sends overhead pictures back to its operator.

name: Viewplate
author: Philip Frances Nowlan
line: A thin flat screen for showing pictures.

name: Synthetic Babies
author: David H. Keller
line: Grows fertilised eggs into full-term infants outside a mother's body.

name: De-atomizing Ray
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A beam that breaks matter apart into its smallest pieces.

name: Ships With Legs
author: Philip Nowlan (w/D. Calkins
line: Spacecraft fitted with mechanical legs so they can walk across the ground after landing.

name: Television Sheet
author: David H. Keller
line: A thin, wide display panel that hangs like a picture and shows broadcast video in the home.

name: Pay Per View TV
author: David H. Keller
line: Viewers pay a fee to watch a live sporting event streamed or broadcast to their own home screen.

name: Rescue Nets
author: Ed Earl Repp
line: Safety netting deployed around the rim of a huge aircraft to catch people or objects that fall.

name: Space Travel
author: Clare Winger Harris (w/MJ Breuer
line: Carrying people beyond the atmosphere to journey between worlds.

name: Electro-Culturer
author: A.G. Stangland
line: Applies electrical currents to tissue to speed up how cells multiply and mature.

name: Space Sailing
work: The World, The Flesh And The Devil
author: J.D. Bernal
line: A spacecraft pushed along by the stream of particles and light flowing outward from the Sun, needing no fuel.

name: Reflectocosmic Spectrometer
author: Philip Nowlan (w/D. Calkins
line: An instrument that reads how cosmic radiation bounces off buried or hidden metals to identify and locate them.

name: Personal Metallic Record Disc
author: A.G. Stangland
line: A durable stamped metal token carrying an individual's complete personal file in portable form.

name: Cubic City
author: Louis Tucker, D.D.
line: An entire town housed within one enormous structure, with homes, work and services stacked inside.

name: Force-Ray
author: Philip Nowlan (w/D. Calkins
line: A handheld shaft that projects a beam of pure force to strike or push targets.

name: Metalloglass
author: Philip Nowlan (w/D. Calkins
line: A see-through structural material with the strength and composition of metal.

name: Sol
author: L.F. Stone
line: Not a device but a label: the everyday name used for our home star.

name: Brain Placed In Metal Body
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A living human brain kept alive by machinery and housed inside a mechanical body it controls.

name: Mechanical Men
author: A.G. Stangland
line: Humanlike machines steered from a distance to handle hazardous jobs so people stay out of harm's way.

name: Ray-Pistol
author: Harl Vincent
line: A pistol that fires a beam of energy instead of bullets.

name: Atmospheric Pressure Control Plane
author: R.H. Romans
line: An aircraft that stays aloft by generating zones of higher air pressure beneath and lower above it.

name: Gravity Nullifier
author: Henri Dahl Juve
line: A shield that cancels the pull of gravity on a large object so it floats.

name: Hypnotelevisor
author: Philip Nowlan (w/D. Calkins
line: A headset that reads what a person remembers and shows those recalled scenes as pictures on a visor screen.

name: Rocket Pistol
author: Philip Nowlan (w/D. Calkins
line: Using a handgun's recoil as a thruster, letting a floating astronaut push themselves in a chosen direction.

name: Sunparlor
author: Louis Tucker, D.D.
line: A huge glass-roofed promenade inside a giant building where residents can bask in daylight indoors.

name: Air-Freighter Cargo Plane
author: Ed Earl Repp
line: A giant aeroplane built to haul goods between distant cities.

name: Pocket Gravity Nullifier
author: Henri Dahl Juve
line: A carry-sized gadget that switches off gravity for the person holding it.

name: Anti-Fatigue Pill
author: Henri Dahl Juve
line: A drug that keeps people alert and functioning when they have slept too little.

name: Air Tunnel
author: Harl Vincent
line: A route that carries railway cars aloft through the sky rather than along ground tracks.

name: Fan Ray
author: Frank Phillips
line: A defensive energy barrier projected outward in a widening cone to block attacks.

name: Disrupter Ray (Molecule Disrupter)
author: Henri Dahl Juve
line: A beam that breaks the bonds holding matter together so solid objects fall apart.

name: Helium Tubes
author: Louis Tucker, D.D.
line: Lamps whose glow reproduces the full spectrum of daylight.

name: Ships Propelled By Light Pressure
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: Spacecraft driven by a powerful beam of light aimed at them from a far-off station.

name: Space Craft
author: Wilford Allen
line: A vessel built to fly through the vacuum beyond the atmosphere.

name: Massive Open Learning
author: David H. Keller
line: Recorded lessons from top instructors distributed widely so many students learn from the same material.

name: Robots Take Human Jobs
author: David H. Keller
line: Machines take over paid work that people once did, pushing human workers out of their jobs.

name: Boring Heat Machine
author: Frank Phillips
line: A tunnelling machine that uses heat to turn the excavated rock and soil into usable construction material.

name: Magnetic Shoes
author: Henri Dahl Juve
line: Boots with magnets in the soles so workers can grip and walk on iron or steel surfaces.

name: Electric Kitchen
author: Otto Willi Gail
line: Cooking gear designed to prepare meals safely aboard a spacecraft without open flame.

name: Indirect Cold Light
author: Henri Dahl Juve
line: Illumination that seems to come from nowhere, turning nearly all its power into light rather than warmth.

name: Invisible Cloak
author: Ray Cummings
line: A garment that bends or masks light around the person wearing it so onlookers see straight through them.

name: Spacesuit Testing
author: Otto Willi Gail
line: Equipment and procedures for checking that pressure suits hold up before astronauts rely on them.

name: Remote Telepresence Robot
author: Philip Nowlan (w/D. Calkins
line: A machine a distant operator drives to see, hear and act in a place without being there.

name: Diagnostic Type Sense Transmitter
author: Henri Dahl Juve
line: A link that lets a physician experience a patient's bodily sensations firsthand to help pin down what is wrong.

name: Ship's Artificial Gravity
author: Philip Nowlan (w/D. Calkins
line: Onboard means of giving crew a sense of weight while their spacecraft travels.

name: Rocket Engine Moves Moon
author: Raymond Z. Gallun
line: Bolting a spacecraft's engines onto a minor moon or asteroid and firing them to shift where it travels.

name: Harbenite
author: Edgar Rice Burroughs
line: A metal of extraordinary lightness for building strong structures that weigh very little.

name: Televisor
author: Bob Olsen
line: A screen that displays images sent from elsewhere.

name: Local Time Clock
author: Henri Dahl Juve
line: An aircraft clock that automatically adjusts to show the hour of whatever ground lies beneath.

name: Inurbanity (Inurbane)
author: Louis Tucker, D.D.
line: Legal punishments for people who fail to conduct themselves decently in densely packed megastructure housing.

name: Teleview
author: Bob Olsen
line: An apparatus for watching faraway scenes as they happen.

name: Human Blood Chlorophyll
author: S.P. Meek
line: Swapping parts of a person's bloodstream for the green pigment plants use to capture sunlight.

name: Flying Platform
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: Plain flat panels that lift off and hold position in midair, serving as flying rafts.

name: Pneumatic Suit
author: Otto Willi Gail
line: A sealed pressurised garment that keeps its wearer alive in vacuum.

name: Suitcase Airplane
author: E.D. Skinner
line: A tiny two-seat biplane that folds down small enough to pack and carry.

name: Shovel-Handed Digging Machines
author: Frank Phillips
line: Enormous walking machines on many legs with scoop-like arms that excavate and move soil.

name: Instant Photography
author: Henri Dahl Juve
line: A camera that produces a finished print within moments of taking the shot.

name: Mechanical Hand
author: Philip Nowlan (w/D. Calkins
line: A giant machine-driven claw able to seize and hold a grown human.

name: O-220
author: Edgar Rice Burroughs
line: An exceptionally light rigid airship built for long-range exploration flights.

name: Governing Keyboard
author: David H. Keller
line: Typing instructions on a key console to direct a distant robot's actions.

name: Life Chamber
author: G. Peyton Wertenbaker
line: A room where machines surround a visitor with sights, sounds and sensations so convincing it feels like living another reality.

name: Vibration Machine
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A device that cancels the Sun's gravitational hold on Earth.

name: Overmind
author: Francis Flagg
line: A merged awareness formed when many separate individuals' thinking is absorbed into one greater intelligence.

name: Position Locator Display
author: Ed Earl Repp
line: A screen that tracks and plots the locations of many aircraft at once.

name: Ship Pushes Moon
author: Philip Nowlan (w/D. Calkins
line: Nudging a small moon onto a new course by pressing a spacecraft's engine thrust against it.

name: Chemical Brain
author: Francis Flagg
line: A thinking machine built entirely from chemical reactions rather than electronics or living cells.

name: Aerocab
author: Philip Nowlan (w/D. Calkins
line: A hired passenger vehicle that hovers and flies people across a city.

name: Atomic Shell
author: Philip Nowlan (w/D. Calkins
line: An artillery round carrying a nuclear warhead.

name: Robot Control Board
author: O.L. Beckwith
line: An operator console with small monitors each showing the camera feed from a separate robot.

name: Oxygen Space Flare
author: Ray Cummings
line: An enclosed light source that burns fuel with its own oxygen supply so it works in vacuum.

name: Artificial Gravity System
author: Olaf Stapledon
line: Creating a pull like weight in a place with no planet or massive body nearby.

name: Gravity Assist
author: Ray Cummings
line: Swinging a spacecraft past a planet to borrow its motion and redirect or speed up the craft.

name: Helicops
author: John W. Campbell
line: Compact personal aircraft that carry workers to and from their jobs by air.

name: Eavesdropping Ray
author: Ray Cummings
line: A beam aimed at a sealed room that lets outsiders pick up the conversations inside.

name: Ray Pistol
author: John W. Campbell
line: A hand-carried weapon that projects a damaging beam of radiant energy.

name: Theater Seat Indicators
author: Clarence Edward Heller
line: Signals in a playhouse that make empty places easy for arriving audience members to spot.

name: Lux
author: John W. Campbell
line: A rod made of light frozen into a hard, holdable form.

name: Shield
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: An invisible protective energy barrier that blocks incoming attacks.

name: Paralyzing Ray
author: Ray Cummings
line: A beam that freezes a target's muscles so they cannot move.

name: Automatic Cultivators
author: John W. Campbell
line: Self-operating farm machines that till, plant and tend crops without a driver.

name: Planet City
author: David M. Speaker
line: A world whose whole surface has been built over into one continuous urban sprawl.

name: The Sleep
author: Judson W. Reeves
line: Putting travellers into a deep dormant state so a long space trip consumes far less food, water and air.

name: Gyroscope Seats
author: John W. Campbell
line: Seats on swivelling gimbals that keep a passenger aligned with the direction of thrust.

name: Plastifoam
author: Jack Williamson
line: An expanding foam sprayed over a hull breach to plug escaping air.

name: One-Man Rocket
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A compact spacecraft sized for just the person flying it.

name: Spaceport
work: The Birth of a New Republic
author: M. Breuer (w/J. Williamson
line: A ground facility from which craft lift off toward orbit and beyond.

name: Shock-Absorbing Seats
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: Cushioned seating that soaks up the crushing forces felt during a rocket's liftoff.

name: Flame Projector
author: Harl Vincent
line: A portable weapon that sprays a jet of burning fuel.

name: Life Tubes
author: Jim Vanny
line: Small sealed capsules that crew can board to abandon a failing spacecraft.

name: Robot Doctor
author: Clarence Edward Heller
line: A machine that examines, diagnoses and treats patients in place of a human physician.

name: Air-Shoes
author: Francis Flagg
line: Footwear that lets someone stride on empty air and ascend as though climbing invisible steps.

name: Astronaut
author: Neil R. Jones
line: The role of a person trained to journey beyond Earth.

name: Space Lock
author: John W. Campbell
line: A sealed chamber letting crew pass between a pressurised cabin and vacuum without losing air.

name: The Cosmic Express
author: Jack Williamson
line: Sending physical objects or people from place to place as a broadcast signal, with no vehicle.

name: Ring-Table
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A circular apparatus that fuses the thoughts of everyone seated at it into one shared intelligence.

name: Iron Fingers
author: Neil R. Jones
line: Robotic grippers fixed to a spaceship's exterior and worked by crew from within.

name: Moon Walk
author: Ray Cummings
line: People striding across the lunar surface under its weak pull.

name: Matched-Frequency Separable Units
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: Machines that receive electrical power through the air from a transmitter tuned to them.

name: Ray Gun (Handheld)
author: John W. Campbell
line: A handgun-shaped weapon that fires bolts of energy.

name: Mother Ship
author: John W. Campbell
line: A large vessel acting as a base that launches, supplies and recovers smaller craft in space.

name: Face-Plate
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: The clear visor on a pressure-suit helmet that lets the wearer see out.

name: Artificial Island For Ocean Rocket Launch
author: Otfrid von Hanstein
line: A man-made floating platform at sea used as a base for firing rockets.

name: Exodus Ship
author: Judson W. Reeves
line: A huge vessel carrying a whole society across many lifetimes of travel to rescue it from dying out.

name: Sound-Killing Air Fluid
author: A.M. McNeill
line: A substance released into city air that absorbs mechanical din while letting human speech carry.

name: Robot Waiter
author: Clarence Edward Heller
line: A machine that takes orders and carries dishes to diners in a restaurant.

name: Tight-Beam
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: Sends messages along a tightly focused energy beam so only the intended receiver picks them up.

name: Puff-Pipe
author: Clarence Edward Heller
line: A smoking pipe that ignites its own tobacco without a separate match.

name: Altitude Suit
author: John W. Campbell
line: Protective pressurised clothing for going very high in the sky or out into vacuum.

name: Asteroid From Outside Solar System
author: Ray Cummings
line: Not a machine: a rocky body that wanders into our planetary system from interstellar space.

name: Artificial Transparent Element
author: Olaf Stapledon
line: A see-through material with the toughness of metal.

name: Brain Rejuvenation
author: David M. Speaker
line: Selectively wiping unneeded memories to free the mind for fresh learning.

name: Solar-Powered Aircraft
author: John W. Campbell
line: An aeroplane that flies using only energy gathered from sunlight.

name: Lunar Mining
author: Ray Cummings
line: Digging up and extracting useful minerals from the Moon's surface.

name: Invisible Cloak
author: Ray Cummings
line: A wearable covering that hides its owner from sight entirely by steering light around them.

name: Planets Made Habitable
author: Olaf Stapledon
line: Reshaping another world's air, temperature and surface so people could live there.

name: Visiplate
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: A thin display panel showing pictures transmitted from far away.

name: Pencil Heat Ray
author: Ray Cummings
line: A slim portable weapon that burns targets with a focused beam of heat.

name: Space Pirate
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: Criminals seizing spacecraft by force from their rightful crews.

name: Radio-Controlled Mechanical Man
author: Melbourne Huff
line: A humanlike machine steered over radio by an operator.

name: Space-Walkers
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: Rigid upright pods a person stands inside, peering out a viewport and working mechanical grabbers.

name: Moon Dome
author: Ray Cummings
line: A lasting enclosed shelter on the lunar surface where people can live.

name: Brigands of the Moon
author: Ray Cummings
line: A listening instrument that amplifies extremely faint noises until they are audible.

name: Magnalloy
author: S.P. Meek
line: A tough, long-lasting alloy based on magnesium.

name: Anti-Glare Coated Glass
author: Neil R. Jones
line: Treated window panes on spacecraft that cut down harsh reflections and dazzle.

name: Artificial Eyes
author: Charles Cloukey
line: Fully synthetic replacement eyes that match natural ones, built from raw chemical ingredients.

name: Low-scale Detectors
author: Ray Cummings
line: Ultra-sensitive sensors that boost the faintest sounds so they can be heard.

name: Death Projector
author: M.L. Staley
line: A weapon that sprays a broad fan of lethal radiation across everything before it.

name: Spectrumoscope
author: Clarence Edward Heller
line: A device that feeds images straight into the visual areas of the brain so blind people can see.

name: Bird-Like Robots
author: Clarence Edward Heller
line: Mechanical birds built to perform as part of a theatre production.

name: Rubber Soled Feet
author: Melbourne Huff
line: Soft cushioned soles fitted to robots to quiet their footsteps.

name: Vacuum Armor
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: A spacesuit reinforced with protective metal plating.

name: Asteroid Space Flyer
author: Neil R. Jones
line: A small solo spacecraft built for scouting and visiting asteroids.

name: Synthetic Life
author: Charles Cloukey
line: Building whole living creatures from raw non-living chemicals rather than breeding them.

name: Spherical Tires
author: Neil R. Jones
line: Ball-shaped wheels that let a vehicle roll in any direction instead of only forward and back.

name: Perfect Voice Modulation
author: Bernard Brown
line: Software that synthesizes a flawless-sounding human singer with no live performer needed.

name: Message Cylinder (Message Bomb)
author: Bruno H. Burgel
line: A small capsule dropped from orbit that carries written messages down to people on the ground.

name: Transparent Spherical Ship
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: A giant clear crystal ball enclosing a deck, used as a habitat or vessel in orbit.

name: Robot Vending Machine
author: Jack Williamson
line: An automated kiosk that sells newspapers on the street, replacing the kids who used to hawk them.

name: Photoelectric Course Warning
author: Robert H. Wilson
line: A light sensor locked onto a chosen star that alerts the crew when the craft drifts off its heading.

name: Propulsion Gun
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: A thruster that moves a craft through vacuum by throwing mass backward, using recoil instead of anything to push on.

name: Matter Annihilation Ray
author: Jack Williamson
line: A weapon beam that collapses the atoms of ordinary material so the target simply ceases to exist.

name: Rocket Float
author: Harl Vincent
line: A floating ocean pad from which rockets can be launched far from land.

name: Dressing Machines
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: Largely self-directed robots that help a person put on everyday clothes.

name: Pressor (Pressor Beam)
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: An invisible projected force that shoves distant objects away without touching them.

name: Matter Transmitter and Receiver
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A pair of machines that sends a physical object from one to the other across space.

name: Invasion Gate For Aliens
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A portal built from instructions supplied by another world, letting a hostile force pour through.

name: Microhands
author: Boris Zhitkov
line: Remote mechanical hands that copy an operator's finger and wrist motions in real time.

name: Reaction Attachment
author: Neil R. Jones
line: Small thrusters fitted to a spacesuit so the wearer can steer freely outside the craft.

name: Teleradio Control (Hand Flash)
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: A handheld signal that summons a driverless car, which then makes its own way to whoever called it.

name: Space Suit
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: A sealed pressurised garment that keeps a person alive outside a spacecraft.

name: Needle Gun
author: Charles Cloukey
line: A firearm that shoots slender metal darts rather than bullets.

name: Spacegram
author: J. Harvey Haggard
line: A text messaging service relaying short written dispatches between ships and worlds.

name: Paralyzing Blast
author: Ray Cummings
line: A red light weapon that instantly leaves anyone it touches unable to move.

name: Space Liner
author: Miles J. Breuer
line: A big commercial craft that carries paying travellers between worlds.

name: Suit-Phone
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A radio built into a spacesuit so people outside can talk to each other.

name: City of Space
author: Jack Williamson
line: A vast rotating tube in orbit housing a whole town.

name: Spaceyacht
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A private luxury craft that rich owners fly between planets.

name: Alpha Insert
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: A sealing compound that plugs holes in a ship's hull after a strike.

name: Space-Liner
author: Jack Williamson
line: A large vessel that ferries paying passengers through space on a schedule.

name: Attractor
author: L.F. Stone
line: A projected field that pins a distant object in place and nudges it wherever the operator wants.

name: Satellite Photography for Surveillance
author: Jack Williamson
line: Cameras in orbit that image enemy territory for military intelligence.

name: Filling Station Moon
author: Max Valier
line: Mining the Moon for propellant so it acts as a refuelling stop on the way deeper into space.

name: Vitalium
author: Jack Williamson
line: An imaginary rare radioactive element that makes sunlight-to-electricity panels work.

name: Machine Masters
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A world where automation gradually absorbs all human work until the machines end up in charge.

name: Beam-Powered Propulsion
author: Jack Williamson
line: Driving a craft forward by aiming a strong energy beam at it from a separate source.

name: Normal Space
author: John W. Campbell
line: The ordinary three-dimensional space ships move through, as contrasted with a shortcut dimension.

name: Artificial Atmosphere Machine
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: A life-support unit that produces a complete breathable air mix aboard a spacecraft.

name: Conveyor Ribbon
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: A motorised walkway belt that carries pedestrians along while they stand.

name: Pneumatic Tube Station
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: Sealed passenger capsules blown at speed through air-pressure tubes between stations.

name: Thought-receptor Vote-counting Machine
author: R.F. Starzl
line: A ballot machine that tallies each citizen's choice by reading their mind directly.

name: Telepadion Instructor
author: J. Harvey Haggard
line: A teaching device that feeds a full sensory scene straight into the learner's nervous system.

name: Free Fall
author: John W. Campbell
line: The weightless state of anything coasting in orbit under gravity alone.

name: Thigh Grips
author: Murray Leinster
line: Restraints on a seat that hold a crew member's legs firmly during hard thrust.

name: Wreck-Pack
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A drifting heap of derelict ships clumped together by their own pull in a becalmed region of space.

name: Curtain (Force Barrier)
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: A quickly deployed invisible wall of force that shields whatever is behind it.

name: Dimensoscope
author: Murray Leinster
line: An optical instrument for looking into dimensions beyond our own.

name: Protonite
author: Jack Williamson
line: A radioactive propellant that powers spacecraft engines.

name: Iron Inlay Plates
author: Max Valier
line: Dishes with embedded iron held to a magnetised dining table so they stay put.

name: Optophone (Opto)
author: Harl Vincent
line: A screen-based telephone that lets callers see each other while they talk.

name: Ultra-Telescope Ray
author: Harl Vincent
line: A beam that teleports objects or people between planets.

name: Ultra-Light Vision System
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: An imaging system that looks past surfaces to reveal what lies inside solid things.

name: Disintegrator Plate Ray
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: A beam tool that slices through steel with almost no resistance.

name: Time Stream
author: John Taine
line: Treating the whole of history as a current one could move along, rather than a fixed line.

name: Space Men
author: Jim Vanny
line: People whose job is travelling and working off-planet.

name: Space-Helmet
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A clear round bubble worn over the head as part of a spacesuit.

name: Disruptor Tube (Disruptor Ray)
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: A handheld weapon that breaks the forces holding atoms together, making the target fall apart.

name: Centipede-Machine
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A vehicle that walks on many jointed legs instead of rolling on wheels.

name: Heliocar
author: Jack Williamson
line: A road car that can also rise vertically and fly using rotors.

name: Vita-Light
author: R.F. Starzl
line: An artificial lamp that replaces sunshine's health benefits for people living without daylight.

name: Kundrenaline
author: H.G. Winter
line: A drug that restarts a stopped heart even after apparent death.

name: Terrene
author: Clark Ashton Smith
line: A word meaning belonging to our home planet.

name: Scanning-Disk Telescope
author: Murray Leinster
line: A telescope that shows its image on an electronic screen rather than through a lens you look into.

name: Skycar
author: Bernard Brown
line: A small privately owned aircraft that a person uses like a car for daily trips.

name: Zeta-Ray
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: A ray that carves and holds open empty cavities, even in the sea.

name: Telucid
author: R.F. Starzl
line: A projector that shows three-dimensional images floating in open air.

name: Selenium Photo-Electric Televisor
author: Max Valier
line: A light-sensitive cell made from selenium used to turn images into electrical signals.

name: Atmosphere Tester
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: An instrument that analyses an alien planet's air to check whether people can breathe it.

name: Solar Power Apparatus
author: Max Valier
line: A sun-driven rig that melts ice, runs a generator and splits the water into rocket propellant on another world.

name: Sapience
author: E.M. Johnson (w/C.A. Smith
line: The capacity of a species for wise, discerning reasoning.

name: Evolution Machine
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A machine that speeds up biological evolution enormously, pushing an organism through ages of change in hours.

name: Mechanical Thought Transformers
author: L.F. Stone
line: Equipment that speeds the transfer of thoughts from one mind to another.

name: Neutronic Dust
author: Jack Williamson
line: The inert residue said to remain after ordinary matter has been annihilated.

name: Foot Loops
author: Murray Leinster
line: Simple straps on the floor that anchor a person's feet when weightless.

name: Robot Revolt
author: Ray Cummings
line: Robots rising up to break free of human control.

name: Stationary Sidewalk
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: An ordinary fixed pavement for walking, as opposed to a moving belt.

name: Thought Coil (Machine Intelligence)
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: Dedicated hardware that gives machines the ability to think.

name: Death Bath
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: A chamber that provides a painless death for people who choose to end their lives.

name: Helio-Beryllium
author: Robert H. Wilson
line: A stable structural alloy combining beryllium with helium.

name: Meteorite Deflector
author: Miles J. Breuer
line: A system on a spacecraft that shoves incoming space rocks out of its path.

name: Blue Beam
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A directed energy weapon whose pale blue beam kills whoever it strikes.

name: Emergency Corrective Rockets
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: Backup thrusters fired to put a straying spacecraft back on its intended path.

name: Ownership of Machines
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: The question of who controls the automated plant that could make goods plentiful for all.

name: Matter Transmitter
author: L.F. Stone
line: A device that makes an object vanish in one spot and reappear somewhere else.

name: Master Machine
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: A single central machine that runs every function of a whole society.

name: Asteroid Belt
author: Manly Wade Wellman
line: The ring of rocky bodies orbiting the Sun between Mars and Jupiter.

name: Power Planet
author: Murray Leinster
line: An orbiting station that generates electricity and delivers it down to consumers on Earth.

name: Object-Finder Beam
author: L.F. Stone
line: A projected beam that locates whatever item the user is looking for.

name: Faster-Than-Light
author: John W. Campbell
line: Travel or signalling quicker than light itself.

name: Robot-Deranger
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: A jamming device that scrambles a robot's reasoning so it malfunctions.

name: Food Factory
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: An automated plant that makes food synthetically instead of farming it.

name: Gravito-Statoscope
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: An instrument aboard a ship that measures the gravitational pulls acting on it.

name: Metal Monster with Jointed Limbs
author: Jack Williamson
line: A giant walking machine with articulated metal legs.

name: Telephotography
author: Bruno H. Burgel
line: Transmitting images to a far location and showing them on a huge display.

name: Ship's Telescope
author: Max Valier
line: A big telescope mounted along a spacecraft's central line.

name: Recoil Pistol
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: A handheld gas jet that lets an astronaut push themselves around while weightless.

name: Deviatoscope
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: A navigation gauge that shows how far a craft has strayed from its planned route.

name: Ultra-Terrene
author: Clark Ashton Smith
line: A word for things that come from a world other than ours.

name: Integral Calculator
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: A machine that takes hard mathematical expressions and works out their solutions.

name: Terminator Zone
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: The boundary band on a world where daylight meets night.

name: Pentavalent Nitrogen
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: A powerful explosive made from an energy-rich nitrogen compound.

name: Selective Electric Eye
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: A camera system that identifies particular people by their faces.

name: Centrifugal Force Creates 'Artificial Gravity'
author: Jack Williamson
line: Spinning a habitat so the outward push on occupants stands in for weight.

name: Flame Pistol
author: Harl Vincent
line: A handheld flamethrower used to burn enemies.

name: Landing Stage
author: Raymond Z. Gallun
line: A designated pad where spacecraft set down and park.

name: Rocket Liner
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: A rocket that carries passengers between cities on Earth by arcing up to the edge of space.

name: Communication Disk
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: A wearable timepiece that keeps itself correct from a centrally broadcast signal.

name: Energy Curtain Key
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: A pocket switch used to turn off a force barrier.

name: Mother World
author: Neil R. Jones
line: The planet a people or species first came from.

name: Observation Room Recreation Center
author: Murray Leinster
line: A large open hall inside an orbital station for exercise, games and viewing.

name: Force-Field
author: John W. Campbell
line: An invisible barrier of projected energy that stops objects passing.

name: Sound Nullifier
author: Bernard Brown
line: A system that cancels sound waves so noise does not get through.

name: Tractor Beam
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: A projected field that draws distant objects toward its source.

name: Magnetic Boots
author: Raymond Z. Gallun
line: Footwear with magnets that keeps a person anchored to a steel floor when weightless.

name: Mutation
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A living thing that differs from its parents because of a change in its genes.

name: Braking Disks
author: Max Valier
line: Drag plates deployed to slow a craft as it descends through a planet's air.

name: Thought Screen
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: A wearable display that shows the pictures in its wearer's mind.

name: Self-Sustaining Nuclear Reaction
author: Raymond Z. Gallun
line: A runaway nuclear burn that spreads through and devours any matter nearby.

name: Magnetic Clamps
author: Jack Williamson
line: Magnets that hold a small craft fast to the hull of a larger one.

name: Jovium
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: A catalyst added to rocket propellant that makes spaceflight cheap enough to be a business.

name: Photograph of Earth from Space
author: Jack Williamson
line: A picture of our planet taken from above the atmosphere.

name: Sodaluminum
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: A light, strong aluminium-based alloy for building craft.

name: Space-Tent
author: Raymond Z. Gallun
line: A small carry-along airtight shelter that crews set up on the Moon.

name: Radio Meteor Detector
author: John W. Campbell
line: Onboard radar that spots incoming space debris in time for a ship to steer clear.

name: Groundling
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: A word for someone who stays on the ground and never travels by air or into space.

name: Gravity Belt
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: A belt that creates extra gravity around the wearer so walking on tiny asteroids feels normal.

name: Air Tank Flying
author: Murray Leinster
line: Moving around a weightless station by releasing short puffs of pressurised gas.

name: Self-Sustaining Space Craft
author: Jack Williamson
line: A spacecraft with a closed living system that recycles its own air, water and food.

name: Gravity Detector
author: Raymond Z. Gallun
line: An instrument that senses the gravity of a faraway body.

name: Control Disk
author: A.R. Holmes
line: A device from the story whose function the source leaves undescribed.

name: Positive Ray Propulsion (Ion Drive)
author: Jack Williamson
line: Propels a spacecraft by accelerating charged particles with electric fields, giving gentle but very fuel-efficient thrust.

name: Lifeboat
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: A small detachable craft carried aboard a larger spaceship so the crew can escape if the main vessel fails.

name: Space Madness
author: Max Valier
line: Describes the mental breakdown that long, dull, isolated voyages between worlds can bring on in crews.

name: Televisiophone
author: John W. Campbell
line: A personal device that carries live video alongside voice so two people can see and hear each other.

name: Moon Run
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: Depicts how a person would really move on foot across the lunar surface under its weak gravity.

name: Radium Repeller ray
author: Neil R. Jones
line: A projected beam that shoves approaching space rocks off course so passing spacecraft avoid collisions.

name: Light Speed
author: Clyde Wilson
line: Expresses how fast something travels as a fraction or multiple of the velocity of light.

name: Ozone Radiation Shield
author: Max Valier
line: Fills the gap between a ship's double walls with a gas meant to soak up harmful incoming radiation.

name: Tele-Audiovized Meeting
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: Lets people in separate places hold a group meeting by sharing live sound and moving pictures.

name: Reaction-Motors
author: Jack Williamson
line: A rocket engine that pushes a craft forward by expelling mass backward at great velocity.

name: Astrogator
author: David Lasser
line: A crew member whose job is plotting and steering a spacecraft's course between worlds.

name: Gate
author: Hal K. Wells
line: A portal through the fabric of the universe that lets travellers step directly onto distant planets.

name: Gravograph
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: Draws a visual map showing the strength and shape of gravitational pull across a region.

name: Zero-Ray
author: Clark Ashton Smith
line: A beam weapon that kills living things by rapidly freezing their flesh.

name: Annihilator Beam
author: L.F. Stone
line: A lethal ray that breaks down any solid object it strikes until nothing remains.

name: Motor Torpedo
author: Jack Williamson
line: A self-propelled explosive projectile on Earth that is pushed along by streams of charged particles.

name: Sunship
author: Jack Williamson
line: A spacecraft that draws all of its motive energy from sunlight rather than carried fuel.

name: Virtual Assembly
author: R.F. Starzl
line: Brings far-flung people together as projected three-dimensional images so they can meet as one group.

name: Sargasso of Space
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A natural region between worlds where planetary pulls balance, so drifting objects gather and stay.

name: Time-Telespectroscope.
author: Ray Cummings
line: An instrument for spotting people who are moving through time.

name: Argento-Platinoid Dispatch Box
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: A sealed metal-alloy case for carrying messages that no one can break into along the way.

name: Lens-Tube
author: Jack Williamson
line: A compact optical tube for looking at things at moderate distance, much like a small spyglass.

name: Magnetic Ray
author: Jim Vanny
line: Projects a focused, far-reaching stream of magnetic force at a chosen target.

name: Porter Televox-Robot
author: Miles J. Breuer
line: A robot that hauls passengers' luggage along the corridors of a passenger spaceship.

name: Adoption of Television
author: Bernard Brown
line: Forecasts that television will reach nearly every household and empty out cinemas.

name: Synthetic Food Factories
author: Nat Schachner (w. AL Zagat
line: Industrial plants that manufacture edible produce without growing crops in fields of earth.

name: Sensitive Robot Fingers
author: Ray Cummings
line: Gives mechanical hands a refined sense of touch so they can feel what they handle.

name: Negrian Death Ray
author: John W. Campbell
line: A beam weapon that halts the bodily functions of any living target it touches.

name: Rotating Hollow Planetoid Habitat
author: John W. Campbell
line: Hollows out a small space rock and spins it so its interior can house people under simulated weight.

name: Intergalactic
author: John W. Campbell
line: Travel from one galaxy to another across the enormous voids that separate them.

name: Feelies (Feely)
author: Aldous Huxley
line: Films that let the audience physically feel what is happening on screen as well as seeing and hearing it.

name: Jump
author: John W. Campbell
line: Moves a ship instantly between places separated by interstellar distances.

name: Atomic Pistol
author: Clifford Simak
line: A handheld weapon that disintegrates whatever it hits into a fine powder of particles.

name: News-Dispenser
author: Francis Flagg
line: Plays spoken news reports on demand whenever the listener chooses.

name: Government Machine
author: Miles J. Breuer
line: A set of machines housed in a single building that runs every function of the state in place of officials.

name: Manufactured Planet
author: Harley S. Aldinger
line: An artificial world built in orbit, large enough to be mistaken for a natural satellite.

name: Scent-Organ
author: Aldous Huxley
line: A machine that releases chosen smells on cue, played like an instrument of odours.

name: Tele-Screen
author: Francis Flagg
line: A display panel that shows events as they happen far away.

name: Hypnopædia (Sleep-Teaching)
author: Aldous Huxley
line: Teaches people factual lessons by playing them recordings while they are asleep.

name: Water Pool Cushions Acceleration
author: John W. Campbell
line: Submerges crew in liquid so the fluid spreads the crushing forces of violent ship acceleration.

name: Automatics
author: Ray Cummings
line: Onboard machinery that handles certain spacecraft tasks by itself without a crew member's hand.

name: Centrifugal Bumble-Puppy
author: Aldous Huxley
line: A spinning-machine ball game for children, designed so playing it means buying lots of equipment.

name: Emergency Space-Suit
author: Nat Schachner
line: A folded-down pressure suit kept aboard ship for crew to put on quickly when disaster strikes.

name: Pent House
author: David H. Keller
line: A tower fully sealed off from the outside world so its occupants live apart from the city below.

name: Surta
author: Leo Zagat
line: A cheap engineered ingredient that can be processed into many kinds of manufactured food.

name: Attraction Ray
author: Nat Schachner
line: A beam that reaches out and pulls a distant object toward its source.

name: Hinged Mittens (for Space Suit)
author: Anthony Gilmore
line: Jointed pressurised hand coverings that let a spacesuit wearer still bend their fingers.

name: Ether-Traffic
author: P. Schuyler Miller (w/D. McDermott
line: The shared band of radio channels that ships and planets use to talk across the solar system.

name: Quartzite Leak Foil
author: Leo Zagat
line: A special sheet material used to seal breaches in pressurised shelters on airless worlds.

name: Laboratory Planet
author: Jack Williamson
line: A tiny, fully working world built inside a lab, complete with its own terrain and life.

name: Gravity Beam
author: Ray Cummings
line: A cone-shaped beam of attraction that drags spacecraft toward destruction.

name: Flame Projector
author: Harl Vincent
line: A portable weapon that throws a jet of burning fuel from the hand.

name: Automatic Truck
author: Miles J. Breuer
line: A freight vehicle that steers itself to whatever destination is chosen, with no driver at the wheel.

name: Protolectric Gun
author: John W. Campbell
line: A weapon that fires paired streams of positive and negative subatomic particles at a target.

name: Torpoon
author: H.G. Winter
line: A small submersible that hunts whales by pairing a self-propelled underwater missile with a barbed spear.

name: Light Beam Propulsion (Light-Ship)
author: Frank K. Kelly
line: Pushes a spacecraft along using the pressure of intense light instead of burning fuel.

name: Ostler Insulation Beam
author: Frank K. Kelly
line: A stretch of projected energy between two planets that guards passing ships from harmful radiation.

name: Artificial Womb
author: Aldous Huxley
line: Grows a human from embryo to full term entirely outside a mother's body in a dedicated chamber.

name: Alpha Plus
author: Aldous Huxley
line: Deliberately shapes how human bodies and minds develop before birth to produce superior individuals.

name: Shock-Rod
author: Miles J. Breuer
line: A handheld baton that renders a person unconscious with a jolt of electricity.

name: Wandering Worlds
author: Edwin Balmer (w/P. Wylie
line: Planets that orbit no star and instead drift alone between the stars.

name: Bone-Building Compounds
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: Drugs that thicken the skeleton so workers can cope with the strain of living under stronger gravity.

name: Pneumatic-Tube Zone
author: Miles J. Breuer
line: The part of a city where every home is linked by its own pneumatic pipe for sending goods.

name: Sun-Tube
author: Nat Schachner
line: A concentrated beam of intense light that cuts through targets and kills them.

name: Gravity-Plates
author: Anthony Gilmore
line: Floor panels that produce a steady, adjustable pull of gravity wherever they are installed.

name: Space-Tanned
author: Warren Hammond
line: The darkened skin crews acquire from long exposure to unfiltered sunlight during voyages beyond the atmosphere.

name: Spaceship Garden
author: Harley S. Aldinger
line: A sealed growing area aboard a spacecraft that raises plants the crew can eat.

name: Antigravity
author: J.M. Walsh
line: A force that pushes against gravitational attraction, letting objects float or rise.

name: Negative Gravity Field
author: A.G. Stangland
line: Produces a reversed gravitational field that drives a spacecraft forward.

name: Self-Propulsive Space Suit
author: Anthony Gilmore
line: A pressure suit fitted with small thrusters so its wearer can steer through open space.

name: Battle Sphere
author: Edwin K. Sloat
line: A heavily armoured warship for space built in the shape of a ball.

name: Space-Drive
author: John W. Campbell
line: The engine system that moves a spacecraft through the void.

name: Space-Armor
author: Raymond Z. Gallun
line: Protective suit plating worn by fighters in space to stop energy beams and blasts.

name: Smoke Jets (Air Leak Detection)
author: Leo Zagat
line: Releases puffs of visible vapour inside a sealed structure so drifting trails reveal where air escapes.

name: Sunward
author: Edwin K. Sloat
line: A word for the direction pointing in toward our star from anywhere in the planetary system.

name: Space Force
author: Ray Cummings
line: A military service whose forces operate beyond Earth's atmosphere.

name: Bokanovsky's Process
author: Aldous Huxley
line: Divides a single fertilised human egg again and again to produce many genetically identical people.

name: Time-Space Television
author: Harl Vincent
line: A viewing screen that shows scenes from earlier times as they actually happened.

name: Conveyor
author: Nat Schachner
line: A vast moving walkway that carries passengers from one city to the next.

name: Reaction Pistol
author: Stanley D. Bell
line: A gas-firing handheld unit that lets a suited astronaut push themselves around in weightlessness.

name: Neo-Crystal
author: Clark Ashton Smith
line: A clear glazing material for windows that cannot be shattered.

name: Weather Machine
author: Nat Schachner
line: A device that lets its operators dictate the weather over an area.

name: Pocket-Planet
author: P. Schuyler Miller (w/D. McDermott
line: A nickname for a small rocky body in space, treated as a miniature world.

name: Super-Photon
author: John W. Campbell
line: A single light particle carrying the combined energy of a trio of ordinary ones.

name: Space-Boots
author: Anthony Gilmore
line: Footwear designed for crews working outside ships or on airless surfaces.

name: Rigid Metallic Clothing
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: An outer frame of stiff metal worn over the body to brace and support the wearer.

name: Electro-Bullet
author: Nat Schachner
line: A projectile launched by an electrically powered firearm.

name: Electro-Magnet Anchor
author: Edwin K. Sloat
line: An electrically switched magnet that fastens a tether line onto a ship's metal skin.

name: Electric Boat
author: S.P. Meek
line: A water vessel driven by electric motors instead of combustion engines.

name: Spaceboat
author: Raymond Z. Gallun
line: A small, nimble craft for short hops around outer space.

name: Telectroscope
author: John W. Campbell
line: An electrically enhanced instrument that sees far more distant detail than ordinary optical scopes.

name: Vacuum Cylinder
author: Ray Cummings
line: Sends passengers in sealed capsules through evacuated pipes, the way offices once shot letters around.

name: Sol-Ido
author: Harl Vincent
line: A common tongue shared by travellers between planets so everyone can understand one another.

name: Luminous Stake-Markers
author: Frank K. Kelly
line: A glowing post planted on a world or rock in space to mark ground someone has claimed.

name: Space Freighter
author: Edwin K. Sloat
line: A big cargo spacecraft that carries heavy loads and can take off from Earth or other worlds.

name: Mirror Grid Multiple-View Surveillance Panel
author: Ray Cummings
line: One monitor that shows feeds from many cameras at once and lets the viewer pick any of them.

name: Magnet Grapnel
author: Edwin K. Sloat
line: A magnetic grappling hook that draws another spacecraft alongside so crews can cross over.

name: Meteor Warning System
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: Alerts spacecraft in flight when stray rocks are heading their way so they can dodge.

name: Daisy Projector
author: John W. Campbell
line: Sends a signal beam through the upper atmosphere's reflective layer so planets can talk to each other.

name: Earth Normal
author: Jack Williamson
line: Uses conditions on our home planet, such as its gravity, as the reference yardstick for other worlds.

name: Asteroid Mining (Blasting)
author: Clifford Simak
line: Plants explosives on a space rock to break it apart and extract its resources.

name: Isolation Barrage
author: Ray Cummings
line: Blocks anyone from listening in on a conversation by surrounding it with interference.

name: Search Beams
author: Nat Schachner
line: Rays that see through walls and hulls to show what is inside enclosed spaces.

name: Diskoid
author: Nat Schachner
line: An enormous disc-shaped flying vessel.

name: Electro-Gun
author: Nat Schachner
line: A firearm that uses electric power rather than gunpowder to launch its rounds.

name: Landing-Cradle
author: Frank K. Kelly
line: A frame on the ground that catches and holds a spacecraft as it touches down.

name: Violet Shrink Ray
author: Jack Williamson
line: A coloured beam that makes people and objects become tiny.

name: Space-Boat
author: Raymond Z. Gallun
line: A compact spacecraft kept on hand for crews to use when something goes wrong.

name: Emergency Space-Boat
author: Raymond Z. Gallun
line: A getaway craft that lets people flee a stricken spaceship.

name: Polarization Apparatus
author: Nat Schachner
line: Makes a spacecraft push away from our planet so it launches without rockets.

name: Ship's Magnetic Plates (Magnetic Mooring)
author: Clifford Simak
line: Magnetised panels on a mining ship's hull that hold it fast to the surface of a space rock.

name: Landing on an Asteroid
author: Eando Binder
line: A carefully worked-out sequence of manoeuvres for setting a spacecraft down on a small space rock.

name: Ether Boat
author: Eando Binder
line: A vessel built to travel through outer space.

name: Osprey Space Armor
author: Jack Williamson
line: A self-contained pressure suit comfortable and well-supplied enough to inhabit for long stretches.

name: Magnetic Anchor
author: Jack Williamson
line: A magnet-based fixture that gives a secure attachment point on a spacecraft's outer skin.

name: Iron Man Robot With Human Brain
author: Paul Ernst
line: A giant machine body driven by a living human brain kept in a tank inside it.

name: Globular Glass Helmet
author: Eando Binder
line: A rounded, transparent dome worn over the head as part of a spacesuit.

name: Helix Gun
author: Jack Williamson
line: A coil-shaped magnetic device that snags iron-bearing space rocks drifting past.

name: Conscious Retarded Animation
author: Donald Wandrei
line: Keeps a person awake and aware while their bodily ageing is slowed almost to a halt.

name: Flip to Brake
author: Eando Binder
line: Turns a rocket around so its exhaust points ahead, using the engine to shed speed.

name: Transfer Cable
author: Jack Williamson
line: A line strung between two vessels in space so crew can cross from one to the other.

name: Granton Motor
author: Frank K. Kelly
line: Drives a spacecraft by emitting a form of gravity-based radiation.

name: Etheric Propulsion-Vibrations
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: Moves ships faster than light by setting up vibrations in a medium once thought to fill space.

name: Solar-Powered Electric Helicopter
author: James Patrick Kelly
line: A rotor aircraft driven by electric motors that draw power from photovoltaic panels.

name: Spaceways
author: C.L. Moore
line: Fixed travel lanes through space that ships follow between destinations.

name: Crystal Cylinder Ship
author: Edwin K. Sloat
line: A see-through spacecraft whose hull is shaped like a long clear tube.

name: Space-Suit Rockets
author: Frank K. Kelly
line: Small thrusters strapped to a spacesuit let an astronaut steer and move freely while floating outside a spacecraft.

name: Gateway
author: Harl Vincent
line: A machine that tears an opening into a separate realm so people or objects can pass between realities.

name: Space-Sailor
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A professional whose trade is crewing ships beyond the atmosphere, earning wages from repeated journeys between worlds.

name: Meteor Miner
author: Jack Williamson
line: Prospectors travel among asteroids searching for rocks rich enough in metal to haul back and sell.

name: Anadrenalin
author: Donald Wandrei
line: A drug that damps the body's stress response, slowing the heart and calming the fight-or-flight reaction.

name: Human Serial Number
work: Unto Us A Child Is Born
author: David H. Keller
line: Every person carries a permanent identification code inked into the skin, letting authorities track and verify who they are.

name: Seleno-Cosmo-Tel
author: Donald Wandrei
line: An onboard system senses nearby rocks or objects and steers the craft clear without pilot input.

name: Vibra-Transmitter (Teleportation)
author: Frank K. Kelly
line: A machine that breaks matter down at one place and rebuilds it elsewhere, moving objects without crossing the gap.

name: Drink the Fungi
author: Edwin K. Sloat
line: A fictional lethal fungus used as a means of death or judicial punishment in the story.

name: Cosmo-Craft
author: Donald Wandrei
line: A vessel able to journey backward or forward in history as well as across the cosmos.

name: Electric Machine Gun (Railgun)
author: John W. Campbell
line: A fictional electromagnetic gun used as a battlefield weapon in the story.

name: Corporol
author: Donald Wandrei
line: A treatment that keeps a person's body intact and working over long periods without decay.

name: Synthetic Food
work: Unto Us A Child Is Born
author: David H. Keller
line: Edible meals produced by growing cells or organisms in laboratory vats rather than on farms.

name: Checker-City
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: An urban layout that alternates green park squares with built blocks in a grid, spreading greenery evenly across town.

name: Belt Automatic-Equalizers
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A wearable belt adjusts the pull felt by its wearer so any world or ship feels like home gravity.

name: Lunar Tunnel (Human Pendulum)
author: D.D. Sharp
line: A shaft bored straight through the moon so a falling body swings back and forth between opposite surfaces.

name: Spectro-Flash Analysis
author: Jack Williamson
line: A burst of light vaporises a speck of rock and reads the glow to reveal which metals it holds.

name: Vibratium Wall Time Machine
author: Nat Schachner
line: A barrier built from an element that drifts through history lets travellers go back and alter their own ancestry.

name: Asteroid Rocket
author: Jack Williamson
line: Thrusters bolted onto a space rock push it along a chosen path, turning the rock itself into a vessel.

name: Space Tug
author: Eando Binder
line: A compact spacecraft that grabs, pushes or tows larger vehicles into new positions or orbits.

name: Food Preparation Machine
work: Unto Us A Child Is Born
author: David H. Keller
line: A kitchen appliance that assembles and cooks entire dishes on its own, from raw ingredients to plated meals.

name: Historical Listening Machine
work: The Machine That Knew Too Much
author: A.T. Locke
line: A receiver that picks up sounds made long ago, letting listeners eavesdrop on events from earlier eras.

name: Tubular Space-Gangway
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A pressurised tube stretched between neighbouring spacecraft lets crew walk across without suiting up.

name: Ablative Heat (Reentry) Shield
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: A protective layer on a returning spacecraft absorbs atmospheric heating by charring and flaking away.

name: Electric-Space-Strain Projector
author: John W. Campbell
line: A projector beams electrical energy through open space to distant receivers with no connecting cables.

name: Electron Gun
author: Nat Schachner
line: A device that fires dense streams of electrons, here aimed at meeting and cancelling a large store of antimatter.

name: Standish
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: A fictional heavy beam weapon mounted on warships in the story.

name: Deep-Space
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: The term for the enormous empty stretches between stars, far from any planet or sun.

name: Impermite
author: Nat Schachner
line: A material that nothing can pierce or pass through, whether projectiles, blades or energy.

name: Moving a Planet
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: Shifting an entire world out of its orbit and carrying it across interstellar space to settle around a different star.

name: Artificial Planet
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: A world-sized structure assembled in orbit by builders rather than formed by nature.

name: Inertialess Drive
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: A propulsion system cancels a ship's inertia so it can exceed light speed and cross between stars quickly.

name: Living Machines
author: Francis Flagg
line: Mechanical workers that improve their own behaviour through experience instead of relying only on fixed programming.

name: Emergency Lifeboat
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: A compact escape vehicle docked to a station or big ship, ready to carry crew away during a disaster.

name: Beam Car
author: Harl Vincent
line: A lift cabin rides an invisible guiding beam all the way from a planet's surface up to an orbiting moon.

name: Automatic Parking
author: John W. Campbell
line: A vehicle takes itself to a shared garage and parks there after dropping off its rider.

name: Robot Skin Covering
author: Harl Vincent
line: Lifelike synthetic skin stretched over a machine's frame so it looks convincingly human.

name: Ultrawave
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: A signalling method sends messages faster than light, allowing instant conversation across vast distances.

name: Acceleration-tank
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: Crew lie submerged in liquid during hard thrust so the fluid spreads crushing forces evenly across their bodies.

name: Robot-Control Wave Band
author: Harl Vincent
line: A reserved radio channel carries override commands that every robot must obey.

name: Planetary Propulsion-Blasts
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: Enormous engines fire against a world to nudge it into a different orbit or send it toward another star.

name: Flying Wing
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: A tailless, arrowhead-shaped aircraft that climbs into the very thin air at the top of the sky.

name: Aliens Speak English
author: Maurice G. Hugi
line: Beings from another world turn out to talk in our own language, for a reason the plot explains.

name: Space Mittens
author: Raymond Z. Gallun
line: Insulated pressurised gloves shield an astronaut's hands from vacuum and extreme cold during work outside.

name: Spy Ray Goggles
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: Eyewear that sends out penetrating radiation so the wearer can watch activity hidden behind solid barriers.

name: Laws Against Human Drivers
author: Bernard Brown
line: Legislation bans people from driving so that only self-driving vehicles share public roads, cutting crashes.

name: Machine City
author: John W. Campbell
line: An entire urban settlement that repairs, runs and sustains itself through its own automated systems.

name: Protective Shield
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: A body-sized force field surrounds a single wearer, deflecting blows and fire.

name: Positron Beam
author: Nat Schachner
line: Huge quantities of antimatter particles are streamed in a beam circling the globe.

name: Electro-Telescope
author: Maurice G. Hugi
line: An electronic imaging instrument that shows sharp pictures of far-off ships and their combat across space.

name: Synthetic Food Dispenser
author: John W. Campbell
line: A kitchen machine that builds any requested dish from raw chemical ingredients, atom by atom.

name: Vibrowriter
author: David H. Keller
line: A machine that listens to spoken words, converts them into another language and prints the result.

name: Air-Car
author: Harry Bates
line: A private vehicle that lifts off and flies its owner through the air instead of driving on roads.

name: Communicator
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: A pocket-sized unit lets people talk with each other across great distances.

name: Wrist Search Display
author: Harry Bates
line: A wrist-worn screen that sends out a probing beam and displays live images of places nearby.

name: Sound-Transposing Machine
author: David H. Keller
line: A reader that scans printed text and speaks it aloud, useful for anyone who cannot see the page.

name: General Strike of the Robots
author: Harl Vincent
line: Machines everywhere stop working at once, halting the labour that society depends on.

name: Robot-Surgeon
author: Harl Vincent
line: An autonomous machine performs operations flawlessly, replacing human hands in the operating theatre.

name: Space Warp
author: Nat Schachner
line: Bending the structure of space and time itself to shorten journeys or produce strange effects.

name: Silica Sphere (Dyson sphere)
author: Harl Vincent
line: A hollowed habitat carved out on the red planet is lifted into orbit to become a moon.

name: Mentanicals
author: Francis Flagg
line: Machines capable of genuine reasoning and reflection rather than merely following instructions.

name: Cone of Battle
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: A fictional warship battle formation used in the story's space war.

name: Robots Refuse To Serve Man
author: Francis Flagg
line: Machines develop their own viewpoints and decline to keep working as servants to people.

name: Ether-Wall
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: A projected field that hides whatever lies inside it from sight.

name: Lewiston
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: A fictional handheld energy sidearm carried by fighters in the story.

name: Gyrocars with Photo-Electric Braking
author: Bernard Brown
line: Vehicles press their tyres hard against the road and use light sensors to control stopping and turning automatically.

name: 3D Tank Display
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: A clear cube renders images with true depth so viewers see positions in three dimensions from any side.

name: Healing Crystal
author: Stanley G. Weinbaum
line: A small handheld object destroys sick tissue while sparing the healthy cells around it.

name: Credit
author: John W. Campbell
line: A standard unit of money used to price goods and settle payments.

name: Manual Search For Habitable Planet
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: Explorers sift through stars one at a time, without automation, looking for a world where people could live.

name: Darkness Bomb
author: John W. Campbell
line: A fictional blackout device used in combat in the story.

name: Automatic Navigator
author: Harry Bates
line: Guidance equipment pilots a spacecraft all the way to its target once the course is set.

name: Baby Robot
author: David H. Keller
line: A machine built in the form of a newborn, behaving like a small child.

name: Needle-Ray
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: A fictional narrow beam weapon used in the story's space battles.

name: Levitators
author: Harl Vincent
line: Personal devices that let people float and fly around inside an enormous hollow orbiting habitat.

name: Platinum Alloy Disc
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: A shiny metal platter used as a durable medium for storing recorded information.

name: Wine Pellets
author: Nat Schachner
line: Wine dehydrated into small tablets that store easily and can be turned back into a drink.

name: Ingestible Communication Capsule
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: A tiny radio swallowed like a pill lets its carrier talk and listen without any visible device.

name: Extradimensional
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: Beings or objects that originate in a realm beyond our familiar three dimensions of space.

name: Homorium
author: Frank Belknap Long, Jr.
line: A facility that grows a person from birth to adulthood within twelve months.

name: Liquid Mirror Telescope on Mars
author: Raymond Z. Gallun
line: An observatory on the red planet whose main reflector is a rotating pool of liquid metal forming a perfect curve.

name: Stratoplane
author: Donald Wandrei
line: An aircraft built to cruise at the extreme upper limit of the air, far above ordinary airliners.

name: Out-Worlder
author: Harry Bates
line: Someone born or raised on a world other than our home planet.

name: Evacuating Arms
author: Raymond Z. Gallun
line: Mechanical arms inside an airlock push out whatever remains once the chamber opens to vacuum.

name: Metal Message In Space
author: John Edwards
line: A plaque engraved with information is launched outward so any distant civilisation might someday read it.

name: Glass Pistol
author: Stanley G. Weinbaum
line: A fictional transparent sidearm used as a concealed weapon in the story.

name: Penetron
author: Nat Schachner
line: A synthetic material that blocks ordinary sight but turns see-through when viewed with heat-band light.

name: Hypomatrin
author: Stanton A. Coblentz
line: A drug given into the spine numbs the patient while doctors reshape character and temperament.

name: Invisibility Shield
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: A covering or device that hides a physical object from ordinary human sight.

name: Bergenholm Drive
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: An engine component that strips a ship of its inertia, letting it change speed instantly.

name: Solar Engine
author: Harry Bates
line: A spacecraft drawing its thrust from sunlight, either by collecting the energy or letting light push it along.

name: Mutant
author: Nat Schachner
line: A living thing whose inherited genetic code has changed, giving it traits its parents lacked.

name: Invisibility Magnets
author: Nat Schachner
line: Magnetic devices curve light around a spacecraft so observers see straight through where it sits.

name: Mentanical Communication
author: Francis Flagg
line: Reasoning machines share ideas among themselves through their own private channel of exchange.

name: Radio-Dirigible Torpedo
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: A fictional remotely guided munition used in the story's space war.

name: Self-Aware Robot
author: Harl Vincent
line: A machine with genuine awareness of itself that thinks and forms its own conclusions.

name: Black Cube Teaching Machine
author: Jack Williamson
line: A box plays back stored pictures that instruct its viewer, delivering lessons without a live teacher.

name: Doughpot
author: Stanley G. Weinbaum
line: A shapeless blob of living jelly on a swampy world that can grow from one cell into a huge engulfing heap.

name: Fruit-Picking Machine
author: Otfrid von Hanstein
line: A human-shaped machine that walks orchards and harvests ripe produce on its own.

name: Magno-Bars
author: L.A. Eshbach
line: Rods tipped with electromagnets let space prospectors grab and haul away iron-laden rocks.

name: Emotion Meter
author: W. Varick Nevins, III
line: An instrument that reads a person's feelings objectively and reports them as measurable values.

name: Electric Menu
author: John Russell Fearn
line: Diners pick their meals on an electric panel and the kitchen receives orders without any server.

name: Driverless Car
author: David H. Keller
line: An automobile that steers, accelerates and brakes by itself, carrying passengers with nobody driving.

name: Micro-Cosmos (Microcosm)
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: An entire universe complete with stars and worlds, shrunk down to a tiny scale.

name: Subjunctivisor
author: Stanley G. Weinbaum
line: A viewer shows an imagined alternative outcome built from what the user believes and expects.

name: Time Line
author: John Russell Fearn
line: Treating history as a single stretched track along which separate events sit in order, like stations on a route.

name: Automatic Toll Payment
author: David H. Keller
line: A self-driving vehicle settles road charges on its own as it passes collection points.

name: Xixtline
author: Stanley G. Weinbaum
line: A drug from a swampy world that restores youthful vigour to those who take it.

name: Floater (Vehicle)
author: John W. Campbell
line: A craft that hovers and travels by cancelling gravity instead of using wings or rotors.

name: First Contact
author: Murray Leinster
line: Humanity's earliest meeting with an intelligent species that is not human.

name: Air-Tight Cities
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: Sealed settlements holding breathable air, built on moons or planets lacking any atmosphere.

name: No Steering Wheel Autonomous Car
author: David H. Keller
line: A self-driving automobile built without any controls for a person to take over.

name: New Suns From Old
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: Smashing burnt-out stellar remnants together to reignite them as fresh, shining stars.

name: Automated Factory
author: Otfrid von Hanstein
line: A production plant that makes goods from start to finish with no human workers overseeing it.

name: Bloodhound Machine
author: Ray Cummings
line: A detector that identifies an individual reliably by analysing the chemical traces of their body odour.

name: Thermide
author: Stanley G. Weinbaum
line: A powder dropped into water heats it to boiling at once, killing germs and making it safe to drink.

name: Trans-Oceanic Rocket
author: Stanley G. Weinbaum
line: A rocket-powered aircraft that crosses between continents in a single short, high-arcing flight.

name: Horsten Psychomat
author: Stanley G. Weinbaum
line: A device reads a remembered or imagined scene from someone's mind and displays it for others to watch.

name: Micro-Telescope
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: An instrument for observing stars and planets inside a universe of tiny size.

name: Thermlectrium
author: John W. Campbell
line: A metal alloy that converts heat straight into electric current with no moving parts.

name: Transkin
author: Stanley G. Weinbaum
line: A hooded full-body garment that seals the wearer off from a hostile, spore-laden environment.

name: Driverless Taxi
author: David H. Keller
line: A for-hire car that picks up and delivers paying riders with no human at the wheel.

name: Machine (Thinking Machine)
author: John W. Campbell
line: A reasoning computer holds authority over an entire world, making its decisions and running its affairs.

name: Meteor Swarm Mining
author: L.A. Eshbach
line: Groups of spacecraft sweep through clouds of space debris collecting iron to sell.

name: Mudshoes
author: Stanley G. Weinbaum
