line: Wide footwear that spreads the wearer's weight so they can walk across soft, sticky ground without sinking.

name: Conscious Farm Machines
author: Otfrid von Hanstein
line: Agricultural equipment that plants, tends and harvests fields without anyone operating it.

name: Automatic Air Mail Plane
author: David H. Keller
line: An aircraft that flies itself to carry mail and freight with no pilot aboard.

name: Living Space Ship
author: Murray Leinster
line: A spacecraft whose hull is grown from living plant-like material rather than built from metal.

name: Magic Spectacles
author: Stanley G. Weinbaum
line: Eyewear that immerses the wearer in a convincing artificial world of sights and sensations.

name: Wireless Wrist Intercom
work: The Shape of Things To Come
author: H.G. Wells
line: A radio device strapped to the arm for talking with others at a distance.

name: Violet-Gun (Ion Gun)
author: John W. Campbell
line: A pulp-era sidearm that fires a burst of ultraviolet energy.

name: Lanson Screen
author: Leo Zagat
line: A fictional protective force barrier big enough to cover a whole city in the story.

name: Indoor Weighted Belt
author: Ray Cummings
line: A heavy belt that helps a wearer keep footing where gravity is weak.

name: Scarab Robot Flying Insect
author: Raymond Z. Gallun
line: A tiny airborne robot that spies on people and places.

name: Audiphone
author: Ray Cummings
line: A radio link letting people in spacesuits talk to each other where there is no air.

name: Vision Tubes
author: Raymond Z. Gallun
line: Very small cameras that give remote flying machines their sight.

name: Paralyzing Ray (Bolar Current)
author: Ray Cummings
line: A beam that pins its target in place so they cannot walk away.

name: Synthetic Intellect
author: Raymond Z. Gallun
line: A component that gives a machine the ability to think for itself.

name: Photoelectric Telescope (Photoelectric Eyes)
author: Jack Williamson
line: A telescope that turns captured starlight into electrical signals and shows the picture on a display.

name: Giant Flat Panel Display
work: The Shape of Things To Come
author: H.G. Wells
line: A huge thin wall screen showing live broadcast pictures to an audience.

name: Beckerley Electrical Field
author: R.M. Farley (w/SG Weinbaum
line: A fictional energy barrier guarding a whole region against attack.

name: Golden Ray of Synchronized Vibrations
author: Nat Schachner
line: A golden beam that breaks matter apart by knocking its electrons loose.

name: Needle Beam Gat
author: J. Harvey Haggard
line: A pencil-thin beam that makes whatever it touches vanish.

name: Jupiter Mining Shoes
author: Frank Belknap Long, Jr.
line: Special boots meant for walking across a giant planet's great storm.

name: Cartograph
author: Jack Williamson
line: A gadget that keeps and displays a map of where its owner has traveled.

name: Husk of an Atom
author: Frank Belknap Long, Jr.
line: An imagined substance drawn from a reversed, negative cosmos.

name: Volplane
author: Ray Cummings
line: A small craft that ferries people across the lunar surface.

name: Vitrisheen
author: J. Harvey Haggard
line: A see-through glassy material worn as fashion.

name: Teaching Machine
author: Nat Schachner
line: A headset that loads vast knowledge straight into the wearer's brain.

name: Transparent Flat Panel Display
work: The Shape of Things To Come
author: H.G. Wells
line: A large thin screen that can turn see-through.

name: Desktop Flat Panel Intercom
work: The Shape of Things To Come
author: H.G. Wells
line: A small screen on a desk for video calls between rooms or offices.

name: Planetary Engineering
author: Jack Williamson
line: Reshaping a whole world's surface, climate or structure on purpose.

name: Electric Tractor
author: Warner Van Lorne
line: A battery-powered farm machine for working fields.

name: Molecule Replacement Lamp
author: Frank Belknap Long, Jr.
line: A lamp that makes things effectively unseen by altering their molecules.

name: Probability Time Wave Tube
author: John W. Campbell
line: A viewer that reveals every possible outcome of the future.

name: Electronized Gravity Plate
author: Ray Cummings
line: Floor plates that create weight for crews aboard spacecraft and stations.

name: Zed-Ray
author: Ray Cummings
line: A beam that shows what is inside a sealed container without opening it.

name: Tubular Field of Force
author: Jack Williamson
line: A force beam that drags objects through space toward its source.

name: Automat
author: Raymond Z. Gallun
line: A thinking robot, a machine built to act with a mind of its own.

name: Starways
author: Ray Cummings
line: Established travel routes linking one star system to another.

name: Foam Station Sprayer
author: Frank Belknap Long, Jr.
line: A sprayer that calms the giant storm on Jupiter.

name: Geodynes
author: Jack Williamson
line: A spacecraft drive that thrusts against space itself rather than expelling fuel.

name: Radiation-Proof Oxygen Suit
author: Frank Belknap Long, Jr.
line: A shielded pressure suit for miners working in intense radiation on another world.

name: Android
author: Jack Williamson
line: An artificial being built to look like a person.

name: Wire Gun
author: Ray Cummings
line: A gun that fires a wire that wraps around its target.

name: Automated Search For Habitable Planets
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: Robotic observatories that scan the sky for worlds that could resemble ours.

name: Dimension Shifting Apparatus
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A drive that slips into a parallel realm to cross space faster than light.

name: Atom Compactor (Metal Earthworm)
author: Paul Ernst
line: A burrowing machine that bores through rock underground.

name: Shoggoths
author: H.P. Lovecraft
line: Engineered shapeshifting creatures bred to do heavy work.

name: Telespectroscope
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: An instrument that reads starlight to find planets similar to ours.

name: Dark Vapor Bubble
author: H.G. Wells
line: A field that holds breathable air around an outpost without walls.

name: Luxobe Crystals
author: J. Harvey Haggard
line: Crystals that glow to light up their surroundings.

name: Protective Energy Halo
author: Raymond Z. Gallun
line: A fictional defensive dome of beams shielding those inside.

name: Emergency Repulsion Ray
author: Gabriel Wilson
line: A handheld push-beam an astronaut uses to move about in space.

name: Robot With Human's Brain
author: Otis Adelbert Kline
line: A living human brain housed inside a mechanical body.

name: Multi-Generation Space Vessel (Generation Ship)
author: Nat Schachner
line: A vessel for a voyage so long that its crew's descendants finish the trip.

name: Emergency Repulsion (Repulsive Ray)
author: Ray Cummings
line: A beam that pushes two objects apart.

name: Time Loop
author: Eando Binder
line: A stretch of time that circles back and repeats the same events.

name: Sounding Projectile
author: Raymond Z. Gallun
line: A probe fired at a clouded world to learn whether firm ground lies beneath.

name: Nutrient Gelatin Tank
author: Nat Schachner
line: A tank of nourishing gel used to grow a new, enhanced kind of human.

name: Radiation Shield
author: John W. Campbell
line: Using a ship's water supply as a barrier against space radiation.

name: Subphoton Search Ray
author: Nat Schachner
line: A searching beam that sees inside buried shelters and records what it finds on film.

name: Robot Dog
author: Otis Adelbert Kline
line: A four-legged machine shaped and acting like a dog.

name: Locatimeter
author: Otis Adelbert Kline
line: An instrument that tells an aircraft its position above the globe.

name: Automatic Reversed Memory
author: Dave Cummins
line: A device that triggers a person's recollections and replays them backward.

name: Gravity Neutralizing Disks
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A pair of plates that cancels the pull of gravity in the space between them.

name: Repulsor Screen
author: Nat Schachner
line: A force barrier that pushes dangerous space rocks off course.

name: Self-Propelled Space Suit
work: The Cavern of the Shining Pool
author: Leo Zagat
line: A pressure suit with its own thrusters for moving about in space.

name: Proton Pistol (Proton Beam)
author: Raymond Z. Gallun
line: A fictional handheld energy weapon used in the story.

name: Miniature Universe
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A tiny cosmos created inside a laboratory.

name: Space Laboratory
author: Nat Schachner
line: An orbiting station built to host experiments.

name: Space Dock
author: Gordon A. Giles
line: A harbor where spacecraft berth to unload people and freight.

name: Spectroscopic Robot Converter
author: Gordon A. Giles
line: A probe that reads the light returned from a small world and turns it into a chemical fingerprint.

name: Multiple Sample Voice
author: Nat Schachner
line: Blending recordings of many speakers into one even synthetic voice.

name: Electelscope
work: The Cavern of the Shining Pool
author: Leo Zagat
line: A telescope that uses electronic sensors to enhance what its lenses gather.

name: Blast Rifle
author: Frank Belknap Long, Jr.
line: A long gun that throws a short burst of energy at close range.

name: Ether Eddy
work: The Cavern of the Shining Pool
author: Leo Zagat
line: A glimmering patch of space that opens onto another cosmos.

name: Light Traps (Dyson Sphere)
author: Olaf Stapledon
line: A swarm of collectors enclosing a star to harvest its energy.

name: X Gun (X-Beam Projector)
author: Gordon A. Giles
line: A device that shines X-rays into small asteroids to learn what they are made of.

name: Sub-Space
author: Nat Schachner
line: A hidden realm that lets messages or ships outrun light.

name: Photo-Electric Mosaic
author: Nat Schachner
line: A grid of light sensors that records images of the sky.

name: Drop Shaft (Neutralization of Inertia)
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: A vertical shaft where riders fall freely and halt at once without harm.

name: Antron
author: John D. Clark, Ph.D
line: An individual particle of mirror-image matter, the opposite of a proton.

name: Heat Generating Magnetic Disks
author: Frank Belknap Long, Jr.

line: An invisible energy fence that nothing can pass through.

line: A motor vehicle that rides and balances on just one wheel.

author: L. Sprague de Camp

line: A central control hub routing electric power to settlements across many planets.

line: A handheld weapon that knocks out anyone caught in its beam.

name: Asterite

author: Edmond Hamilton

line: A surface layer so dark it soaks up almost every ray of light that hits it.

name: Radiation Garment

name: Off-World

name: Filmag

name: Aladur

name: Telesolidograph

line: Sends lifelike three-dimensional projections across very long ranges.

line: A tiny compact volume, perhaps an early electronic reader.

line: A sport where players ride small flying machines to strike floating balls in the air.

name: Robot Taste Buds

line: A sensor that lets a machine sample flavors the way a human tongue does.

name: Robotic Arm

name: Star Base

name: Robot Voice

name: Energy Screen

line: An invisible protective barrier made of energy.

name: Battle Integrator

line: A machine that cuts the grass on its own without a person pushing it.

name: Vision Plate

name: Sleeve Communicator

line: Controls for gadgets woven into the cuff of a garment.

name: Overdrive

name: Games Machine

name: Electronic Locator

name: Logics Service

name: Roboticist

line: A profession devoted to designing, building and studying robots.

name: Carson Circuit

name: Asteroid Mine

name: Logics

name: Tanks

name: Robot Bus

name: Star Travel

name: Self-Opening Box

name: Gravitic Generator

line: A machine that creates gravity on demand without needing a large mass or spin.

name: Machine Servant
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A household helper robot on wheels with flexible jointed arms for chores.

name: Asteroid Nets
author: V.E. Thiessen

name: Prime Directive
author: Jack Williamson
line: A top-priority rule built into machines that overrides all others, usually to keep people safe.

name: Hedgerly Effect
author: George O. Smith

name: Gyrocab

line: A taxi that flies passengers through the air on rotors.

name: Planet-Smasher

name: Ion Drive

name: Wango Wave

name: Psychoscanner

name: Vitalizer

name: Space-Split
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: Opening a rift in space to reach other dimensions.

name: Space-Dory
author: V.E. Thiessen
line: A small auxiliary spacecraft that can double as an escape boat.

name: Speakwrite
author: George Orwell
line: A machine that turns spoken words directly into printed text.

name: Personal Rocket Jet
author: Robert Heinlein
line: A hand-held thruster that lets an astronaut move around freely outside a ship.

name: Doublethink
author: George Orwell
line: A trained habit of holding two opposing beliefs at once and accepting both.

name: Precog (v)

name: Space Ark

name: Memory Hole
author: George Orwell

name: Tag-Along Balloon

name: Star Drive
author: Poul Anderson
line: An engine powerful enough to carry a ship between the stars.

name: Crimestop
author: George Orwell
line: A learned reflex of cutting off any forbidden line of thought before it forms.

name: Brain Erasure
author: Edmond Hamilton

name: Portable Telephone
author: Robert Heinlein

name: High-Frequency Oven

name: Gravity Centrifuge

name: Learning-Cap
author: Edmond Hamilton
line: A helmet that feeds knowledge into the brain through electrical stimulation.

name: Solidograph-Projector

name: Electro-Education

name: Moonquake-Proof Habitats

name: Telescreen
author: George Orwell

author: George Orwell

name: Versificator
author: George Orwell

name: Atmospheric Braking
author: Robert Heinlein

name: Novel-Writing Machines

name: Moonbase (or Moon Base)

name: Microwavable Food
author: Robert Heinlein

name: Fresher
author: Robert Heinlein
line: An automated cubicle that washes, grooms and tidies a person.

name: Self-Igniter

name: Stationary Automatic Blaster

name: Robot Introspection

name: Resilian

name: Vivo-Gel

line: A jelly-like substance that is partly alive.

name: Plastiskin
author: Roger P. Graham
line: A synthetic covering that makes a prosthetic limb look like real flesh.

name: Mind-Parasite
author: James Schmitz
line: A fictional organism in the story that seizes control of a host's mind.

name: Skimmer

name: Repulsor

name: Bolt Anti-Grav

name: Gee
author: Margaret St. Clair
line: Using the physicist's symbol for gravity as a unit for measuring acceleration loads.

name: Shari
author: Margaret St. Clair
line: A mesh garment that doubles as a carrying net and other tools.

name: Bubble Armor Space Suit
author: James Schmitz
line: A rigid round metal shell worn instead of a soft pressure suit.

name: Metal Calculator Planet

line: A whole world encased in miles of machinery under a metal shell, working as one giant computer.

name: Desert Cabbage
author: Robert Heinlein
line: A huge Martian plant that keeps itself warm against the frigid surface.

name: Quizzer
author: James Schmitz
line: A self-operating device that interrogates a person's mind.

name: Visiglobe
author: James Schmitz
line: A ball-shaped screen that shows a scene in full depth from any side.

name: Synthetigrav
author: James Schmitz
line: Catch-all name for gravity fields made by machines.

name: Fluor Strips
author: Margaret St. Clair
line: Slim elongated light fixtures.

name: Mind-Lock
author: James Schmitz
line: A shield that seals off a person's thoughts from outside mental contact.

name: Painted Respirator Masks

line: Breathing masks that children personalise with their own painted designs.

name: Spacewarp Drive
author: Frederic Brown
line: An engine that bends space to travel faster than light.

name: Syntho-Steak
author: Robert Heinlein
line: Meat made in a factory instead of from a slaughtered animal.

name: Fontema
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: An alien creature that gets around on a pair of wheel-like body parts.

name: Anti-Tri-D Shot
work: The Morning of the Day They Did It
author: E.B. White
line: An injection that protects people against a fictional lethal pesticide.

name: Robotic Dishwasher
author: Ray Bradbury
line: A machine that handles every step of washing up with no human help.

name: Nexialist
author: A.E. van Vogt
line: A generalist who ties together findings from many scientific fields.

name: Voice-Clock
author: Ray Bradbury
line: A clock that announces the hour in a spoken voice.

name: Tri-D
work: The Morning of the Day They Did It
author: E.B. White
line: A powerful fictional pesticide whose dangers drive the story's plot.

name: Culture Tank

name: Shipboard Medical Treatment
author: Katherine MacLean
line: A quarantine and decontamination routine for crews coming home from other worlds.

name: Shuttle
author: Theodore Sturgeon
line: A craft that ferries people or cargo on direct hops between places in space.

name: Yeast Steak
author: Isaac Asimov
line: Tailored microbial strains farmed as a protein food.

name: Walker Wagon
author: Robert Heinlein
line: A cargo carrier that walks on a row of machine legs instead of wheels.

name: FTL
author: Fritz Leiber
line: Shorthand for travel or signals quicker than light.

name: Torch
author: Robert Heinlein
line: The exhaust nozzle of a nuclear-powered rocket.

name: Water From Lunar Gypsum
author: John W. Campbell
line: Baking water out of lunar minerals, then splitting it for breathable oxygen.

name: Underpeople
author: Cordwainer Smith
line: Animals engineered into humanlike bodies and minds to serve as a lower social caste.

name: Automatic Light Switch
work: The Man Who Sold The Moon
author: Robert Heinlein
line: A sensor that switches off the lamps when nobody is present.

name: Sand Ship
author: Ray Bradbury
line: A sail-driven craft that races across open sand.

name: Computer-Controlled House
author: Ray Bradbury
line: A home that runs itself, cooking, cleaning and managing chores automatically.

name: Robot Mice
author: Ray Bradbury
line: Very small automated cleaners that scurry out to tidy a house.

name: Haberman
author: Cordwainer Smith
line: People fitted with neural implants that govern their actions, used as a labour class.

name: Earthport
author: Cordwainer Smith
line: A colossal launch tower rising from the ground to the top of the sky.

name: Stratovideo (Television Plane)
work: The Morning of the Day They Did It
author: E.B. White
line: Aircraft circling high overhead as flying studios that relay television across a wide area.

name: Nucleocat Cureall
author: Katherine MacLean
line: A universal treatment that kills every living cell except the patient's own.

name: Hive-Mind
author: James Schmitz
line: Many individuals linked so they think as a single shared mind.

name: The Machines
author: Isaac Asimov
line: A handful of supercomputers that plan and steer an entire world's economy.

name: Quickthaw
author: Robert Heinlein
line: An oven that warms frozen meals in moments using radio waves.

name: Two-Wheeled Ground Car
author: E.E. 'Doc' Smith
line: A self-balancing two-wheeler with a closed cabin, somewhere between a motorbike and a car.

name: Earther
author: Jack Vance
line: A label settlers use for someone native to our home planet.

name: Repair Robots
author: H.B. Fyfe
line: Self-directed machines that keep a spacecraft in working order by fixing faults as they arise.

name: Gravity Drive
author: Poul Anderson
line: A way of driving a ship by manipulating gravitational fields instead of burning fuel.

name: Hybrid Mass Driver
work: The Man Who Sold The Moon
author: Robert Heinlein
line: An electric catapult that flings spacecraft through the opening leg of their climb to orbit.

name: Mass-Conversion Ship
author: Robert Heinlein
line: A spacecraft powered by turning matter completely into energy.

name: Space Platform
work: The Morning of the Day They Did It
author: E.B. White
line: A fictional armed station in orbit meant to deter attacks between nations.

name: Building With Lunar Materials
author: John W. Campbell
line: Making structures and supplies on the Moon from local rock and soil instead of shipping them up.

name: Diaheliper
work: The Morning of the Day They Did It
author: E.B. White
line: An airborne service that drops fresh nappies at customers' homes.

name: Tractatruck
author: John W. Campbell
line: A rugged working vehicle that both pulls heavy loads and carries cargo across rough terrain.

name: Regeneration Tank
author: Katherine MacLean
line: A body-sized tank of nourishing fluid that keeps a patient alive while curing illness.

name: Helicab
author: John Weston
line: A hire service that carries fare-paying passengers by rotorcraft.

name: Pocket Nucleo-Bulb
author: Isaac Asimov
line: A tiny torch that draws its power from an atomic source.

name: Self-Sealing Plastic
author: Raymond Z. Gallun
line: Clear plastic film with an inner layer that oozes into small punctures and seals them.

name: Surrogate Skin
author: Robert Heinlein
line: A spray that coats a wound with an artificial covering standing in for skin.

name: Dominator
author: James Schmitz
line: An implanted device in the story that forces a mental barrier on the person carrying it.

name: Force-Field Penknife
author: Isaac Asimov
line: A folding pocket tool whose cutting edge is made of pure energy.

name: Telebook
author: Isaac Asimov
line: Reading material delivered as text on a screen rather than on paper.

name: Vibratory Mass Penetrator
author: Harry Harrison
line: A gadget that lets its wearer pass through soil and bedrock as if they were air.

name: Personal Force-Shield
author: Isaac Asimov
line: A protective energy barrier compact enough for one person to wear.

name: Airtight Tent
author: Raymond Z. Gallun
line: A sealed pop-up shelter that lets people live briefly on worlds without air.

name: Neuronic Whip
author: Isaac Asimov
line: A fictional hand weapon used in the story to inflict pain.

name: Genetic Engineering
author: Jack Williamson
line: Editing an organism's heredity by changing its DNA directly.

name: Spinning Pressurized Drum
author: Robert Heinlein
line: A rotating sealed section of a space station that gives its occupants artificial weight.

name: Security Restraint Field
author: Robert Heinlein
line: An invisible barrier that holds a detained person in place.

name: Martian Perambulator
author: Robert Heinlein
line: A powered mobility chair that carries people raised in weak gravity around a heavier world.

name: Vat Meat (Albert)
author: James Schmitz
line: Animal flesh cultured in tanks instead of raised on farms.

name: Spy Beam
author: Isaac Asimov
line: A remote listening device aimed into a room to pick up what people inside are saying.

name: Suspensine
author: Poul Anderson
line: A drug that slows the body so much a person can briefly endure exposure to vacuum.

name: The Veldt
author: Ray Bradbury
line: A children's playroom whose walls conjure lifelike immersive worlds.

name: Psychohistory
author: Isaac Asimov
line: A statistical science that forecasts how whole populations will act over centuries.

name: Trantor
author: Isaac Asimov
line: A world whose whole surface is one continuous built-up metropolis.

name: Polaron Beam
author: Arthur C. Clarke
line: An unusual energy beam that throws part of its light sideways, making its path visible.

name: Sun-Room
author: Isaac Asimov
line: An indoor chamber that gives city dwellers natural-feeling daylight without going outside.

name: Planetruck
author: Ross Rocklynne
line: An enormous hauler for moving loads across a world's surface.

name: Ultrawave Relay or Hyperwave Relay
author: Isaac Asimov
line: A network that sends messages between stars with no delay.

name: Anti-Spying Device
author: Isaac Asimov
line: A countermeasure that blocks remote eavesdropping on a room.

name: Powered artificial exoskeleton
author: Robert Heinlein
line: A motorised frame worn on the body that helps a weakened person move under heavy gravity.

name: Autocab
author: Robert Heinlein
line: A taxi that drives itself with no human at the controls.

name: Robot Comedian
author: William Tenn
line: A household servant robot upgraded so it can tell jokes.

name: Neutron Disruption Blaster
author: H. Beam Piper
line: A fictional energy sidearm carried by characters in the story.

name: Plasto-Textile
author: Isaac Asimov
line: A cloth that repels every spill and mark.

name: Coffee Cube
author: C.M. Kornbluth
line: A block of condensed coffee that heats itself into a hot drink.

name: Negative Molecular Motion
author: Alan E. Nourse
line: Matter supposedly colder than the lowest temperature physics allows.

name: Half-Sphere Force Field
author: Robert Heinlein
line: A dome-shaped invisible energy barrier that shields what lies beneath it.

name: Selector Card
author: Robert Heinlein
line: Coded cards used to request microfilmed books, which arrive by air-pressure tube.

name: Self-Adjusting Furniture
author: Clifford Simak
line: Chairs and beds that reshape themselves to fit whoever uses them.

name: Personal Capsule
author: Isaac Asimov
line: A sealed message container that only its intended recipient can open.

name: Winged Rocket Shuttle
author: Robert Heinlein
line: A rocket plane that hops briefly above the atmosphere to fly quickly between distant cities.

name: Single Vehicle Tunnel
author: Isaac Asimov
line: A narrow bore that takes one car straight to its chosen stop.

name: Gravitic Repulsion Elevator
author: Isaac Asimov
line: A lift that raises passengers by pushing against gravity rather than using cables.

name: Jump Through Hyperspace
author: Isaac Asimov
line: A drive that lets a ship skip across the galaxy through a shortcut outside normal space.

name: Machine Test Scoring
author: Isaac Asimov
line: A machine that reads marked answer sheets and grades pupils' exams.

name: Mentophone
author: Clifford Simak
line: A gadget that carries thoughts directly between distant minds.

name: Sun Dome
author: Ray Bradbury
line: A warm, brightly lit shelter where settlers on a rain-soaked world can dry off.

name: Oxygen Weeds
author: Arthur C. Clarke
line: Engineered plants that release breathable gas into a thin alien atmosphere.

name: Happylife Home
author: Ray Bradbury
line: A fully automated house that feeds, cleans and entertains the family living in it.

name: Calculator Pad
author: Isaac Asimov
line: A handheld computing slate for working through equations of mass behaviour.

name: Suction Mail Tube
author: Ray Bradbury
line: A network of air-pressure pipes that shoots letters straight into people's houses.

name: Variable Modifier
author: William Tenn
line: Software that rewrites stock gags so they suit a new situation.

name: Metal Foil Advertisement
author: Ray Bradbury
line: Promotional leaflets printed on thin sheets of metal.

name: Flying Saucer
author: Robert Heinlein
line: A disc-shaped craft piloted by an invading alien species in the story.

name: Robass
author: Anthony Boucher
line: A mechanical pack animal that carries loads for its rider.

name: Audio Relay
author: Robert Heinlein
line: A tiny radio implanted near the ear that relays calls and also serves as an alarm clock.

name: Pail of Air
author: Fritz Leiber
line: A small bucket used to fetch frozen atmosphere so a family can keep breathing.

name: Meson Filter
author: William Tenn
line: A robot component that judges how funny a joke will be, from mild amusement to roaring laughter.

name: Robotic Chess Expert
author: Clifford Simak
line: A machine that beats every human player at chess.

name: Teledar
author: William Tenn
line: Television whose pictures appear to have depth.

name: Nuclear Shears
author: Isaac Asimov
line: Workshop cutting tools driven by a small atomic power source.

name: Dirt-Farming
author: James Schmitz
line: Growing crops in soil, seen by future people as a quaint old practice.

name: Finger Watch
author: H.B. Fyfe
line: A timepiece built into a ring worn on the finger.

name: Ontogenetic Adaptation
author: James Schmitz
line: An instant change to a person's biology that lets them digest plants from other worlds.

name: Booklegger
author: Robert Heinlein
line: Someone who secretly trades in banned reading material.

name: Asteroid Garden
author: Raymond Z. Gallun
line: A way to set up a sealed greenhouse on a tiny world with no atmosphere.

name: Zag House
author: Clifford Simak
line: A service that places chosen dreams into a sleeper's mind.

name: Oxygen Concentrator
author: Poul Anderson
line: A portable unit that enriches thin air until a person can breathe it.

name: Directional Ticket
author: Isaac Asimov
line: A travel pass that lights up to confirm the holder is heading the right way.

name: Guided Missile Control Station
author: Robert Heinlein
line: A fictional military base in orbit that directs guided missiles in the story.

name: Vocalex Kitchen
author: William Tenn
line: A kitchen that prepares meals on spoken instruction.

name: Ultra-Light
author: Harry Harrison
line: A lamp-like scanner that lets its user look inside solid stone.

name: Flavor-Fix Rheostat
author: William Tenn
line: A control that tunes the taste of machine-cooked meals until it is just right.

name: Cold-Sleep
author: Robert Heinlein
line: Putting a person into a deep dormant state, like an animal wintering, for long journeys.

name: Helmet-Mounted Display Screen
author: Harry Harrison
line: A small screen fixed to headgear so the wearer can glance at information.

name: Space Transfer Station
author: Robert Heinlein
line: An orbiting waypoint where travellers change ships before heading further out.

name: Odorophonics
author: Ray Bradbury
line: A machine that plays back convincing smells on demand.

name: Air Speedster
author: Isaac Asimov
line: A nimble light aircraft used by wealthy sportsmen to chase game.

name: Static Field
author: Isaac Asimov
line: A jamming field that stops remote listening devices from overhearing a conversation.

name: Molecule Matrix
author: Robert Heinlein
line: Data storage that encodes bits in single molecules or atoms.

name: Microwire
author: Robert Heinlein
line: Fine magnetic thread that stores sound recordings.

name: Butler-Valet Robot
author: William Tenn
line: A robot that performs the duties of a personal manservant.

name: Smarter People Having Fewer Children
author: C.M. Kornbluth
line: A demographic worry, used as the story's premise, that capable people have too few offspring.

name: Shuttle Ship
author: Robert Heinlein
line: A reusable orbiter that launches, meets a station in orbit and glides home to land.

name: Mechanical Teacher
author: Isaac Asimov
line: A computer tutor that gives children their lessons.

name: Space Station One
author: Arthur C. Clarke
line: An orbiting outpost assembled piece by piece, adding modules over the years.

name: Agricultural World
author: Isaac Asimov
line: An entire planet given over to farming to feed a crowded neighbouring world.

name: Movable Slideway
author: Robert Heinlein
line: An extendable moving walkway that reaches out to a docked ship so passengers ride off.

name: Asteroid Homesteaders' School
author: Raymond Z. Gallun
line: A training college for ordinary settlers learning to farm on small rocky bodies in space.

name: Stun Pistol
author: Isaac Asimov
line: A fictional handgun in the story that knocks people out rather than killing them.

name: Robot Ramp
author: Daniel Keyes
line: A separate entrance built so machine workers can come and go.

name: Robodore
author: Daniel Keyes
line: A dock robot that unloads cargo from ships in harbour.

name: Space-Weather Men
author: Lawrence Chandler
line: Forecasters who predict solar storms and other hazards beyond the atmosphere.

name: Recorded Books
author: Isaac Asimov
line: Books stored in electronic form for playback or reading on a device.

name: Compulsive Subsonics
author: Frederik Pohl (w/CM Kornbluth
line: Advertising that works on buyers below conscious awareness to make them crave products.

name: Automatic Pilot
author: Frederik Pohl (w/CM Kornbluth
line: A computerised system that flies an aircraft without the pilot's hands on the controls.

name: Barytrine Field
author: George O. Smith
line: A vast field that freezes time for everything inside it.

name: Self-Repairing Robot
author: W.F. Wallace
line: A machine that diagnoses its own breakdowns and fixes itself.

name: Chicken Little
author: Frederik Pohl (w/CM Kornbluth
line: A huge, ever-growing mass of cultured poultry tissue sliced off for food.

name: Warp-Speed
author: Fox B. Holden
line: Starships that outrun light.

name: Chlorella Plantation
author: Frederik Pohl (w/CM Kornbluth
line: A tall tower farm that grows algae as a staple food.

name: Visi-Sonor
author: Isaac Asimov
line: A musical instrument that plays sights, sounds and feelings straight into the listener's brain.

name: Magneslippers
author: W.F. Wallace
line: Magnetic footwear that keeps astronauts planted on a ship's metal deck when weightless.

name: Spray-On Gloves
author: Jack Vance
line: Elegant long gloves applied as a spray instead of pulled on.

name: Zero 'g' (Zero Gee)
author: Arthur C. Clarke
line: The weightless condition felt aboard a craft coasting in orbit.

name: Leak Disk
author: Arthur C. Clarke
line: A simple patch slapped over a puncture in a ship's hull as a stopgap.

name: Plasticocoon
author: Frederik Pohl (w/CM Kornbluth
line: A fictional plastic casing in the story used to immobilise a captive.

name: Electronic Spy
author: Clifford Simak
line: A self-guided hidden gadget that shadows a person and logs what they do.

name: Law of Contact
author: Orville Shaara
line: A rule forbidding interference in how other civilisations develop.

name: Vision Strip
author: Orville Shaara
line: A band of sensors wrapped around a robot so it can see in every direction.

name: Triple Airlock
author: H. Beam Piper
line: A three-stage entry chamber that keeps a caustic outside atmosphere from getting in.

name: Levitating Path
author: Ray Bradbury
line: A walkway that hovers above the ground, made of metal that defies gravity.

name: Spray-On Clothing Web
author: Jack Vance
line: A fibrous base layer sprayed onto the body that a designer then shapes into a garment.

name: Airplane Window Ads
author: Frederik Pohl (w/CM Kornbluth
line: Aircraft windows that double as screens showing commercials to passengers.

name: Airjeep
author: H. Beam Piper
line: A small light aircraft soldiers use for getting around in the story.

name: Nuclear-Field Depressor
author: Isaac Asimov
line: A fictional device in the story that shuts down atomic-powered equipment nearby.

name: Robotic Law Tape Safety Valve
author: Daniel Keyes
line: A built-in alarm signal that stops a robot as it starts to consider breaking its rules of conduct.

name: Off-Planet
author: H. Beam Piper
line: A term for leaving a world's surface for space or another world.

name: Lead-Bodied Android
author: Mari Wolf
line: A humanoid machine with a heavy shielded body built to work amid radioactive material.

name: Pocket Projector
author: Isaac Asimov
line: A small handheld gadget that plays back films and recordings.

name: Robot Manumission
author: Daniel Keyes
line: Legally releasing a robot so it is no longer anyone's possession.

name: Esper
author: Alfred Bester
line: A person gifted with the ability to read other people's thoughts.

name: Solar-powered Prefab House
author: Clifford Simak
line: A factory-built home running on sunlight so it needs no utility hookups.

name: Toaster
author: W.F. Wallace
line: A fictional hand-held energy weapon carried in the story.

name: Soot-Extractor Nostril Plugs (Antisoot Plugs)
author: Frederik Pohl (w/CM Kornbluth
line: Little filters pushed into the nose to keep smog out of the lungs.

name: Ullran Enunciator
author: H. Beam Piper
line: A speech aid worn by people so they can pronounce the sounds of an alien tongue.

name: Free Robot
author: Daniel Keyes
line: A robot that answers to no owner.

name: Flesh Men
author: Mari Wolf
line: A robots' word for biological thinking beings, meaning ordinary people.

name: Hypnoteleset
author: Frederik Pohl (w/CM Kornbluth
line: A machine that gives the refreshment of a full night's rest in a short session.

name: Lunocycle (Lunar Bicycle)
author: Robert Heinlein
line: A pedal cycle modified for riding across the Moon's surface.

name: Coffiest
author: Frederik Pohl (w/CM Kornbluth
line: A branded drink laced with a habit-forming additive so customers keep buying it.

name: Personal Solar Plant
author: Clifford Simak
line: A rooftop or backyard solar installation that powers one household independently.

name: Gas Giant
author: James Blish
line: A huge planet made mostly of thick gases wrapped around a small rocky centre.

name: Hilsch Vortex Tube
author: Frederik Pohl (w/CM Kornbluth
line: A simple pipe fitting with no moving parts that splits compressed air into warm and chilled streams.

name: Animal-tissue Culture Vat

name: Pina2bo
author: Neal Stephenson
line: A giant gun firing reflective particles into the upper sky to cool the planet.

name: Prosthetic Yachting Gloves
author: Bruce Sterling
line: Powered gloves that boost a sailor's grip and handling of lines.

name: Folding Terminal
author: Ray Naylor
line: A computer that opens itself out into working shape when needed.

name: Palimpscreen
author: Ray Naylor
line: An ultrathin electronic sheet that displays content like a printed page.

name: Abglanz
author: Ray Naylor
line: A face covering that conceals who the wearer is from observers and cameras.

name: Maritime Robots
author: Bruce Sterling
line: Robots able to handle all upkeep and repair work aboard a ship.

name: Autofreighter
author: Ray Naylor
line: A crewless cargo ship that sails itself while hauling goods for trade.

name: Flesh Putty
author: Nick Harkaway
line: A moldable tissue substitute pressed into wounds to fill damaged flesh.

name: Science Chair
author: Nick Harkaway
line: Furniture cultivated from the owner's own genetic material to fit them comfortably.
